TABATABAI:12:22-34#26/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#26/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#26/r3.claim: Fear-based worship chiefly motivates avoiding forbidden acts, hope-based worship motivates good deeds, but love directs both toward God Himself and purifies the heart’s attachments.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#26/r3.anchor: عبادته تعالى خوفا من العذاب تبعث الإنسان إلى التروك

TABATABAI:12:22-34#27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#27/r1.claim: Divine love is the light and spirit that guides a person to good works, explaining why the lover does only what is beautiful and avoids evil.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#27/r1.anchor: وهذا هو السر في أنه لا يقع منه إلا الجميل والخير ويتجنب كل مكروه وشر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.claim: “Death” means a life of disbelief and “life” a life of belief; the light is God’s Book, revealed in 6:114–119 to distinguish right from wrong, while layers of darkness are the speculations and innovations of 6:116 and 6:119.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.anchor: The word “death” refers to the life spent in disbelief and “life” refers to life spent in belief.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.claim: The parable contrasts believers given faith and scripture with people wandering in superstition; it encourages believers to ignore human and jinn devils’ clamour and carry the message of life forward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.anchor: to encourage the believers that they no longer should they pay heed to this clamour

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.claim: Those given God’s light must seek guidance from it and present it publicly so others can benefit; light is meant to illuminate people’s path, not be hidden.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.anchor: when someone is blessed with light from God, his obligation towards it is to obtain guidance from it and also present it before other people

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.claim: The statement that disbelievers’ deeds seem fair reassures the Prophet not to despair over those who choose darkness; people are surrounded by what they like, a law discussed further at 6:125 and the beginning of al-Baqarah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p115.anchor: the law of God is that what people like surrounds them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r1.claim: He says the verse was revealed about Ḥamza and Abū Jahl: after Abū Jahl threw filth at the Prophet, Ḥamza returned from hunting, struck him with his bow, rebuked idol worship, and accepted Islam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في حمزة وأبي جهل رمى الرسول بفرث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r2.claim: Another report from him says the verse concerns ʿAmmār and Abū Jahl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا أنها نزلت في عمار وأبي جهل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r3.claim: He says it concerns ʿUmar and Abū Jahl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r3.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: في عمر وأبي جهل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r4.claim: After describing believers and disbelievers, God compares a believer who was once an unbeliever to a living person moving by light, and the unbeliever to someone trapped in darkness, making their difference clear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r4.anchor: شبه المؤمن بعد أن كان كافرا بالحي المجعول له نور يتصرف به كيف سلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r5.claim: Death, life, darkness, and light are figurative here: death and darkness denote unbelief, while light denotes faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r5.anchor: والموت والحياة والنور والظلمة مجاز فالظلمة مجاز عن الكفر والنور مجاز عن الإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r6.speaker: الماتريدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r6.claim: He interprets death as the unseen, unreasoning state in the womb before birth; the believer is then brought from darkness into sight of truth, unlike one left in it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r6.anchor: الموت مجاز عن كونه في ظلمة البطن لا يبصر ولا يعقل شيئا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r7.speaker: ابن بحر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r7.claim: He offers a related interpretation: a person began as a sperm, clot, or morsel of flesh, then was formed and given spirit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r7.anchor: قال: أو من كان نطفة أو علقة أو مضغة فصورناه ونفخنا فيه الروح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r8.claim: The light may mean wisdom, religion, or the Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r8.anchor: وأما النور فهو نور الحكمة أو نور الدين أو القرآن أقوال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r9.claim: He defines life as readiness to receive universal knowledge and light as reasoning from first principles to theoretical unknowns; walking among people means attending to sacred knowledge and spiritual insights.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r9.anchor: الحياة الاستعداد لقبول المعارف فتحصل له علوم كلية أولية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r10.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r10.claim: Alternatively, life is the soul's capacity and light is its connection to revelation; discernment requires a sound intellect and revelation as sight requires a sound eye and sunlight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r10.anchor: الحياة الاستعداد القائم بجوهر الروح والنور اتصال نور الوحي والتنزيل به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r11.claim: Al-Razi's elaborated philosophical account is far from the idiom and ordinary meanings of Arabic speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p634/r11.anchor: وهو بعيد من مناحي كلام العرب ومفهوماتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r1.claim: God attributes the believer's benefits to Himself, while the disbeliever's state is phrased without attribution; darkness is plural because forms of unbelief vary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r1.anchor: نسب ذلك إليه فقال: فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا وفي صفة الكافر لم ينسبها إلى نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r2.claim: The believer carries light wherever he goes; in public it illuminates both himself and others, so his benefit exceeds himself, unlike the disbeliever fixed in darkness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r2.anchor: يمشي به في الناس أي يصحبه كيف تقلب، وقال: في الناس إشارة إلى تنويره على نفسه وعلى غيره من الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r3.claim: The bāʾ in ليس بخارج منها strengthens the image of the disbeliever's settled inability to leave darkness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r3.anchor: وأكد ذلك بدخول الباء في خبر ليس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r4.claim: He rejects identifying the light and darkness with the resurrection light and Hell's darkness, although that interpretation invokes the verse about their light moving ahead and to the right.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r4.anchor: ويبعد قول من قال: إن النور والظلمة هما يوم القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r5.claim: The reading attributed to Ṭalḥa begins أفمن with faʾ instead of wāw.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p635/r5.anchor: وقرأ طلحة أفمن الفاء بدل الواو

QASHANI:6:120-122/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:120-122/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:120-122/r3.claim: The one who was dead represents the soul in ignorance and veiled by its own attributes; bringing it to life means knowledge and love of the Real, or unveiling the veils of its attributes through divine disclosures.

QASHANI:6:120-122/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:120-122/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:120-122/r4.claim: The granted light may be God's guidance and knowledge, light from divine attributes, or light from God's sustaining presence in the Essence, according to the recipient's rank.
QASHANI:6:120-122/r4.anchor: من هدايتنا وعلمنا أو نورا من صفاتنا أو نورا منا بقيوميتنا له بذاتنا

QASHANI:6:120-122/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:120-122/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:120-122/r5.claim: The example describes someone trapped in the darkness of the self, its attributes, and its acts, unable to emerge from them.
QASHANI:6:120-122/r5.anchor: في ظلمات من نفسه وصفاتها وأفعالها ليس بخارج منها

QASHANI:6:120-122/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:120-122/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:120-122/r6.claim: The veiled are made to see their own deeds as good and remain screened by them.
QASHANI:6:120-122/r6.anchor: كذلك زين } للمحجوبين عملهم فاحتجبوا به

DURR-FULL:v3p351/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r4.claim: The dead person is an unbeliever astray; God guides him, gives him the Quran as light, and contrasts him with one in disbelief and misguidance.
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس {أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه} قال: كان كافرا ضالا فهديناه {وجعلنا له نورا} هو القرآن

DURR-FULL:v3p351/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r5.claim: Mujahid reads death as misguidance, being given life as guidance, the light as guidance, and darkness as lasting misguidance.
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {أو من كان ميتا} قال: ضالا {فأحييناه} فهديناه

DURR-FULL:v3p351/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r6.claim: Ikrimah reports that the verse was revealed about Ammar ibn Yasir.
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس} قال: نزلت في عمار بن ياسر

DURR-FULL:v3p351/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the guided person as Umar ibn al-Khattab and the one trapped in darkness as Abu Jahl.
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس} قال: عمر بن الخطاب

DURR-FULL:v3p351/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the verse compares Umar, whom Islam revived and honored, with Abu Jahl, whom God left in misguidance; it recalls the Prophet's prayer for either man to strengthen Islam.
DURR-FULL:v3p351/r8.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم في قوله {أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس كمن مثله في الظلمات} قال: أنزلت في عمر بن الخطاب

FARRA:v1p352/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p352/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p352/r4.claim: The dead person brought to life was astray and then guided; the light by which he walks among people is his faith.

NAHHAS:v2p93/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p93/r7.speaker: المسيبي عن نافع بن أبي نعيم
NAHHAS:v2p93/r7.claim: Al-Musayyibī reports from Nāfiʿ b. Abī Nuʿaym a reading with the waw vowelless.
NAHHAS:v2p93/r7.anchor: وروى المسيبي عن نافع بن أبي نعيم 122 بإسكان الواو

NAHHAS:v2p93/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p93/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p93/r8.claim: The waw may be read as an interrogative conjunction or understood semantically as “consider whether I should seek a judge other than God,” or as a transition to the one who was dead and revived.
NAHHAS:v2p93/r8.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر يجوز أن يكون محمولا على المعنى أي انظروا وتبينوا أغير الله أبتغي حكما أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه

NAHHAS:v2p93/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p93/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p93/r9.claim: With fatḥa on the waw, it is a conjunction preceded by the interrogative alif.
NAHHAS:v2p93/r9.anchor: ومن فتح الواو جعلها واو عطف دخلت عليها ألف الاستفهام

THALABI:v4p185#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p185#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p185#2/r7.claim: The opening alif is an interrogative attached to the conjunction; the dead person is a disbeliever dead in error whom God guides and chooses through faith, giving him a light for the path.
THALABI:v4p185#2/r7.anchor: قوله تعالى أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه هو ألف الاستفهام والتقدير دخلت على واو النسق

THALABI:v4p185#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p185#2/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v4p185#2/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the light as Islam and connects it with God's bringing people from darkness into light.
THALABI:v4p185#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد: يعني بهذا النور الإسلام نيابة قوله يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور.

THALABI:v4p185#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p185#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v4p185#2/r9.claim: Qatāda says the believer has a light and proof from God by which he acts, follows, and reaches for God's Book.
THALABI:v4p185#2/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: هذا المؤمن معه من الله نورا وبينة يعمل بها ويأخذ وإليها ينتهي كتاب الله

THALABI:v4p185#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p185#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v4p185#2/r10.claim: One view treats the word mathal (“likeness”) in the comparison with someone in darkness as extra, yielding “like one in darkness.”
THALABI:v4p185#2/r10.anchor: قال بعضهم: المثل زائد تقديره كمن في الظلمات.

THALABI:v4p185#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p185#2/r11.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v4p185#2/r11.claim: Another view takes the phrase as an imperative “be,” or as a comparison to someone wandering amid disbelief, ignorance, and error.
THALABI:v4p185#2/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم: معناه كن أو شبه بشيء كان يشبهه من في الظلمات من ظلمة الكفر والجهل والضلالة والمسير.

SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r1.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r1.claim: The hamza in أو من كان may be advanced before the conjunction, the majority analysis, or remain in place with an omitted verb between it and الواو.
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r1.anchor: قد تقدم أن هذه الهمزة يجوز أن تكون مقدمة على حرف العطف وهو رأي الجمهور

SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r2.claim: من is the initial subject and كمن its predicate; يمشي is an adjective of نورا, while مثله is the subject and في الظلمات its predicate within من's relative clause.
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أو من كان }: " أو من كان " قد تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r3.claim: The كاف phrase is the predicate of the first من; ليس بخارج is a circumstantial clause describing the relative person as still settled in darkness.
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r3.anchor: في محل نصب على الحال من الموصول أي: مثل الذي استقر في الظلمات

SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa attaches the circumstantial clause to the pronoun in منها, barring attachment to the ه in مثله because the predicate intervenes; Makkī attaches it to the implicit pronoun in الظلمات.
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r4.anchor: ليس بخارج في موضع الحال من الضمير في

SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r5.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif reads أفمن with فاء instead of واو.
SAMIN-DURR:6:122/r5.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف " أفمن كان " بالفاء بدل الواو.

SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r1.claim: كذلك زين is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun; estimates compare the unbelievers' beautification either with bringing believers to life or with their remaining in darkness.
SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r1.anchor: نعت لمصدر فقدره بعضهم: زين للكافرين تزيينا كما أحيينا المؤمنين

SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r2.claim: The omitted agent of زين may be God or Satan; both are explicitly named as beautifiers elsewhere in the Qur'an.
SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r2.anchor: والفاعل المحذوف من " زين " المنوب عنه هو الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r3.claim: ما كانوا يعملون occupies the نائب الفاعل position; ما may be a relative pronoun, a verbal noun particle, or an indefinite noun described by a clause, with ellipsis of the relative in the first and third analyses.
SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r3.anchor: يجوز أن تكون موصولة اسمية أو حرفية أو نكرة موصوفة

SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses the كاف in the nominative and paraphrases: just as what was related to you, the unbelievers' deeds were beautified.
SAMIN-DURR:6:122#2/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: " موضع الكاف رفع، و المعنى: مثل ذلك الذي قصصنا عليك

ZAJJAJ:v2p288/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p288/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p288/r1.claim: An exegetical view identifies the revived person as the Prophet, given Islam, prophethood, and wisdom, and the one in darkness as Abu Jahl in disbelief.
ZAJJAJ:v2p288/r1.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنه يعني به النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأبو جهل بن هشام

ZAJJAJ:v2p288/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p288/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p288/r2.claim: More generally, the verse applies to anyone God guides or leaves astray: the guided person is like the dead brought to life and illuminated by wisdom and faith.
ZAJJAJ:v2p288/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون هذه الآية عامة لكل من هداه الله ولكل من أضله الله

ZAJJAJ:v2p288/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p288/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p288/r3.claim: The disbeliever is like someone trapped in darkness and unable to escape it.
ZAJJAJ:v2p288/r3.anchor: ومثل الكافر مثل من هو في الظلمات لا يتخلص منها

ASAD-NOTES:6:122#n108/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:122#n108/r1.speaker: all commentators
ASAD-NOTES:6:122#n108/r1.claim: Commentators agree that the one who was dead is metaphorical: a person made spiritually alive through faith who can then navigate life without error.
ASAD-NOTES:6:122#n108/r1.anchor: All the commentators agree in that the expression "he who was dead" is metaphorical, and that it refers to people who become spiritually alive through faith

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p187/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p187/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p187/r1.claim: The bāʾ in a negated predicate of laysa gives a different, firm denial from bare laysa, which may be uttered without full conviction; the passage lists Quranic examples of the bāʾ construction.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p187/r1.anchor: ولا يستوي البيان بهذا الباء، والاستغناء عنها في خبر "ليس" بأسلوب النفي البسيط المعتاد، حين يكون قائل الجملة الخبرية غير مستيقن مما ينفيه

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398/r1.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ alone reads ميتا with the yāʾ geminated.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وحده أو من كان ميتا مشددة

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r1.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r1.claim: The other readers lighten ميتا; Abū ʿUbayda says the light and geminated forms share the same meaning.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r2.claim: The verse describes someone who had been dead in unbelief and whom God found alive through Islam, in contrast with the unbeliever persisting in disbelief.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r2.anchor: أي: صادفناه حيا بالإسلام من بعد الكفر، كالكافر المصر على كفره

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r3.claim: One possible referent of the believer’s light is the eschatological light of believers, which runs before them and to their right on the Day of Resurrection.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما أن يراد به النور المذكور في قوله: يوم ترى المؤمنين والمؤمنات يسعى نورهم

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, the light is the wisdom granted to a Muslim through Islam: the believer is the opposite of the unbeliever placed in darkness.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالنور: الحكمة التي يؤتاها المسلم بإسلامه

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r5.claim: The light reading is the same in meaning as the geminated one; the second of the two yāʾs, originating from wāw, is deleted by regular weak-letter treatment.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p398#2/r5.anchor: والتخفيف مثل التشديد، والمحذوف من الياءين الثانية المنقلبة عن الواو

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p149/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p149/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p149/r1.claim: The verb is read with doubling or without it, as explained earlier; spiritual death means disbelief and revival means faith.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p149/r1.anchor: يقرا بالتشديد والتخفيف وقد ذكرت علته آنفا والمعنى أفمن كان ميتا بالكفر فأحييناه بالإيمان

NASHR:v2p223/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p223/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p223/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar doubles the yāʾ in all the listed forms of «الميتة/ميتا», «بلد ميت», and «الحي من الميت والميت من الحي».
NASHR:v2p223/r6.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بتشديد الياء في جميع ذلك، ووافقه نافع في يس الأرض الميتة

NASHR:v2p223/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p223/r7.speaker: نافع
NASHR:v2p223/r7.claim: Nāfiʿ agrees with Abū Jaʿfar in Yā Sīn’s «الأرض الميتة», al-Anʿām’s «أومن كان ميتا», and al-Ḥujurāt’s dead-brother and dead-land forms.
NASHR:v2p223/r7.anchor: ووافقه نافع في يس الأرض الميتة، وفي الأنعام أومن كان ميتا، وفي الحجرات لحم أخيه ميتا

NASHR:v2p223/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p223/r8.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p223/r8.claim: Yaʿqūb agrees with Abū Jaʿfar and Nāfiʿ in the cited al-Anʿām forms.

QIRAAT-ER:6:122:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:122:4#1/r1.speaker: classical grammarians
QIRAAT-ER:6:122:4#1/r1.claim: Classical grammarians debate whether geminated mayyit means currently dying while simplified mayt means already dead; both are canonical.
QIRAAT-ER:6:122:4#1/r1.anchor: classical grammarians debate whether مَيِّت = currently dying while مَيْت = already dead

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r1.claim: The parable deters Muslims from obeying polytheists after the warning: believers have revelation's light, while polytheists drown in disbelief and error.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r1.anchor: تمثيل مسوق لتنفير المسلمين عن طاعة المشركين إثر تحذيرهم عنها بالاشارة إلى أنهم مستضيئون بانوار الوحي الالهي

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r2.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r2.claim: Al-Tibi connects this verse to the preceding warning, وإذا أطعتموهم.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r2.anchor: كما قال الطيبي متصلة بقوله سبحانه وان اطعتموهم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r3.claim: The hamza is a rebuke; the waw joins a nominal clause to an implied matching clause, as if asking whether the audience is like the dead person made alive.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r3.anchor: لعطف الجملة الاسمية على مثلها الذي يدل عليه الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r4.claim: Along with life, God grants a great light by which the person moves among people, secure from them.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r5.claim: The clause may answer an implied question about what the person does with the light, or serve as an adjective of نور.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r5.anchor: والجملة إما استئناف مبني على سؤال نشأ من الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r6.claim: The first من is a relative pronoun and subject, with its following clause as relative and كمن مثله as the predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r6.anchor: ومن اسم موصول مبتدأ وما بعده صلته والخبر متعلق الجار والمجرور

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r7.claim: On the preferred parse, the second من is relative, مثله is its subject, and في الظلمات has an omitted predicate; ليس بخارج منها is circumstantial and completes the predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r7.anchor: أسم موصول أيضا و ( مثله ) مبتدأ وقوله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r8.claim: Both instances of من may instead be indefinite nouns described by the clauses that follow.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r9.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats في الظلمات as the predicate of مثله without an implied هو; the author prefers an explicit complete clause because a bare locative lacks an apparent subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r9.anchor: كأبي البقاء أن في الطلمات هو الخبر وليس هناك هو مقدرا

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r10.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r10.claim: Abu al-Baqa rejects making ليس بخارج a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in مثله, citing separation and the weakness of a circumstantial clause from a genitive complement.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r10.anchor: جملة ( ليس بخارج ) حالا من الهاء في ( مثله ) ومنعه أبو البقاء

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r11.speaker: نافع ويعقوب
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r11.claim: Nafi and Yaqub read ميتا with a doubled ياء, an original form shortened in the common reading by deletion of the second ya.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18/r11.anchor: قرأ نافع ويعقوب ( ميتا ) بالتشديد وهو أصل للمخفف

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r1.speaker: شيخ الاسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r1.claim: The first composite image represents someone created on Islam's natural disposition and guided by clear signs; the second represents someone fixed in error and unable to leave it.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r1.anchor: مثل ما أريد به من بقي في الضلالة بحيث لا يفارقها أصلا كما أن الأول مثل أريد به من خلقه الله تعالى على فطرة الاسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r2.speaker: القطب الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r2.claim: Al-Qutb al-Razi classifies both comparisons as extended similes, not metaphors.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r2.anchor: ونص القطب الرازي على أنهما تمثيلان لا استعارتان

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r3.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r3.claim: Al-Shihab objects that both are tableau metaphors: the compared subject is not explicitly mentioned, and the first whole image is tenor while the second is vehicle.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r3.anchor: ورد كما قال الشهاب بأن الظاهر بأن من كان ميتا ومن مثله في الظلمات من قبيل الاستعارة التمثيلية

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r4.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r4.claim: The comparison resembles asking whether a lion is like a fox, meaning whether a brave person is like a coward; the author calls the point subtle and memorable.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r4.anchor: وهذا كما تقول في الاستعارة الافرادية أيكون الأسد كالثعلب أي الشجاع كالجبان

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the dead person as an unbeliever, revival as guidance, light as the Quran, and darkness as unbelief and misguidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r5.anchor: والتفسير المأثور عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن المراد بالميت الكافر الضال وبالاحياء الهداية

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r6.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas transmitted by Abu al-Shaykh says the verse was revealed about Umar, who was guided, and Abu Jahl, who remained in darkness.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r6.anchor: على ما أخرج أبو الشيخ عنه نرلت في عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه وهو المراد بمن أحياه الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r7.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r7.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam also relates the occasion as Umar and Abu Jahl.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r7.anchor: وروي عن زيد بن أسلم مثل ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r8.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies the pair as Hamza and Abu Jahl.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r8.anchor: وفي رواية عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنها في حمزة وأبي جهل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r9.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r9.claim: Ikrima identifies the pair as Ammar ibn Yasir and Abu Jahl.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r9.anchor: وعن عكرمة أنها في عمار بن ياسر وأبي جهل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r10.claim: The lesson follows the wording's general scope, including everyone who obeys God and everyone who persists in error and rebellion.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r10.anchor: فالعبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب فيدخل في ذلك كل من انقاد لأمر الله

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r11.claim: كذلك may point back to the beautification already mentioned, to the devils' inspiration of their allies, or to the beautification of faith for believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r11.anchor: إشارة إلى التزيين المذكور على طرز ما قرر في أمثاله أو إشارة إلى إيحاء الشياطين إلى أوليائهم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r12.claim: The beautification may be attributed to God as an act of creation or to the devils through whispering.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r12.anchor: من جهته تعالى خلقا أو من جهة الشياطين وسوسة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p18#2/r13.claim: The unbelievers include Abu Jahl and those like him.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p19/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p19/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p19/r1.claim: The deeds beautified for unbelievers are the many forms of disbelief and sin they persisted in, including the ugly acts already described.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p19/r1.anchor: أي ما استمروا على عمله من فنون الكفر والمعاصي التي من جملتها ما حكي عنهم من القبائح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r1.speaker: نافع والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r1.claim: Nafiʿ geminates the y in mayyitan here, in 49:12, and in 36:33; the other readers pronounce it lightly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع " ميتا " و (لحم أخيه ميتا) (الحجرات، 12) و (الأرض الميتة أحييناها)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r2.claim: The person was astray and dead through disbelief, then God gave him life through guidance and faith.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r2.anchor: {فأحييناه} أي: كان ضالا فهديناه، كان ميتا بالكفر فأحييناه بالإيمان،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r3.claim: One explanation identifies the light as Islam, as in 2:257 where God brings people from darkness to light.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r3.anchor: قيل: النور هو الإسلام، لقوله تعالى "يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور" (البقرة، 257) ،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the light as God's book, a clear proof with the believer, through which he acts, takes guidance, and ends up.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو كتاب الله بينة من الله مع المؤمن، بها يعمل وبها يأخذ وإليها ينتهي،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r5.claim: He walks among people along the straight path.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r5.anchor: {يمشي به في الناس} على قصد السبيل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r6.claim: Al-mathal is an extra grammatical element here, so the phrase means like someone in darkness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r6.anchor: {كمن مثله في الظلمات} المثل صلة، أي: كمن هو في الظلمات،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r7.claim: The darkness from which he cannot emerge is the darkness of disbelief.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r7.anchor: {ليس بخارج منها} يعني: من ظلمة الكفر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the revived man as Hamza and the one in darkness as Abu Jahl: after Abu Jahl defiled the Prophet, Hamza returned from hunting, struck Abu Jahl with his bow, then declared his faith.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: جعلنا له نورا، يريد حمزة بن عبد المطلب، كمن مثله في الظلمات يريد أبا جهل بن هشام، وذلك أن أبا جهل رمى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بفرث

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r9.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse was revealed about ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab and Abu Jahl.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r9.anchor: وقال الضحاك: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب وأبي جهل (2) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r10.speaker: عكرمة والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r10.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Kalbi say the verse was revealed about ʿAmmar ibn Yasir and Abu Jahl.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p184#2/r10.anchor: وقال عكرمة والكلبي: نزلت في عمار بن ياسر وأبي جهل (1) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p185/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p185/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p185/r1.claim: What was adorned for disbelievers is their disbelief and disobedience.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p185/r1.anchor: {كذلك زين للكافرين ما كانوا يعملون} من الكفر والمعصية،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p185/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p185/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p185/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Satan made idol worship appear attractive to them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p185/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد زين لهم الشيطان عبادة الأصنام.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r1.claim: The dead person is an analogy for someone God guided and rescued from error, granting the light of proofs and signs to distinguish truth from falsehood and the rightly guided from the erring.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r1.anchor: مثل به من هداه الله سبحانه وتعالى وأنقذه من الضلال وجعل له نور الحجج والآيات

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r2.speaker: نافع ويعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ and Yaʿqūb read mayyitan in its original form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع ويعقوب { ميتا } على الأصل

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r3.claim: Mathaluhu means his description; it is a subject whose predicate is 'in the darknesses.'
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r3.anchor: كمن مثله } صفته وهو مبتدأ خبره

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r4.claim: The circumstantial clause belongs to the implied pronoun in the locative phrase, not the pronoun in mathalihi, because of the intervening material.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r4.anchor: حال من المستكن في الظرف لا من الهاء في مثله للفصل

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r5.claim: The person still in darkness is the one who remains in error and never leaves it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r5.anchor: وهو مثل لمن بقي على الضلالة لا يفارقها بحال

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r6.claim: Just as faith was made attractive to believers, the deeds of disbelievers were made attractive to them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r7.claim: One report identifies the guided person as Ḥamza and the disbeliever as Abū Jahl.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r7.anchor: والآية نزلت في حمزة وأبي جهل

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r8.claim: Another report identifies the guided person as ʿUmar or ʿAmmār and the disbeliever as Abū Jahl.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:122-123/r8.anchor: وقيل في عمر أو عمار وأبي جهل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706/r1.claim: Biqāʿī frames the exposition from 6:100 to the sūra’s end as a detailed unfolding of its opening call to take God as protector and Creator.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706/r1.anchor: إلى آخر السورة تفصيل لقوله تعالى في أول السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706/r4.claim: The images of being brought to life and of guidance continue the opening declaration that the Prophet was commanded to be the first to submit.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r1.claim: Restating a point in a new style after establishing it with proofs makes it firmer in the soul, especially when the second wording adds clarity and fresh notice.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r1.anchor: كان أثبت في النفس وألصق بالقلب

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r2.speaker: الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r2.claim: Al-Ghazālī argues that Qur’anic repetition is never empty of added benefit; readers should examine what precedes and follows the repeated wording.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r2.anchor: قال الغزالي في أوائل كتاب الجواهر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r5.claim: The warning against obeying polytheists means returning to the darkness of error after receiving guidance; this contrast sets up the verse’s question.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r5.anchor: معنى التحذير من طاعة المشركين أنكم إن فعلتم كنتم قد رددتم أنفسكم إلى ظلام الضلال

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r6.claim: The dead person is immersed in the waves of disbelief’s darkness, possessing no independent life, as if only inertness or nonexistence remained.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r6.anchor: أي بالغرق في أمواج ظلام الكفر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r7.claim: God gives life by making faith’s lights shine on the heart; when the heart is sound the whole body is sound, and when it is corrupt the body is corrupt.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r7.anchor: بإشراق أنوار الإيمان على قبله الذي إن صلح صلح الجسد كله

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r8.claim: The light is guidance to every good; walking by it among people makes his deeds, character, and speech perceptible to them.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r9.claim: Biqāʿī takes the likeness either as an example exposing the represented person’s inner core and heart, or as a description of that person’s state.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r9.anchor: وهو ما ينكشف بوجه الشبه روح لبه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r10.claim: The darknesses are ignorance, the desire that grows from ignorance, and disbelief that grows from desire.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r10.anchor: من ظلمة الجهل وظلمة ما ينشأ عنه من الهوى وظلمة ما نشأ عن الهوى من الكفر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r11.claim: If even the ideal likeness is rooted in darkness, the represented person is more deeply rooted in it; he cannot leave while his beautified deeds are dearer than himself and his property.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r11.anchor: وإذا كان المثل الذي هو الأعلى من الممثول في شيء كان الممثول عريقا فيه بطريق الأولى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r1.claim: The dead and darkness imagery recalls that only those who hear respond, while the deniers are deaf and dumb in darkness.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r1.anchor: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا صم وبكم في الظلمات

BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r2.claim: The devils’ whispering to their allies produces blindness by beautifying vile acts.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r2.anchor: إيحاء الشياطين إلى أوليائهم مما يوجب لزوم العمى ليس إلا تزيينا للقبائح

BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r3.claim: The answer to the astonishing self-harm of unbelievers is that God has made their deeds attractive to all unbelievers through the disposition formed in them.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r4.claim: The verse uses paralleled omission: being in darkness is stated first to imply it again, and beautification is stated second to imply it at first.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p707/r4.anchor: أثبت أولا كونه في الظلمات دليلا على تقديره ثانيا

BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r1.claim: Burning incense, sprinkling rosewater, or sacrificing where jinn are suspected is shirk; sacrifices meant to imitate a rooster or protect one's family and property from jinn are also directed to jinn.
BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r1.anchor: وقد ظهر لك من هذا كله أن إحراق البخور ، وإلقاء ماء الورد ، ورشه وذبح شيء من مكان يتوهم فيه الجن ، كله شرك

BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that after Abū Jahl threw dung at the Prophet, Hamza struck Abū Jahl with his bow, defended the Prophet, denounced stone worship, and accepted Islam; the verse was then revealed.
BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r2.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أن أبا جهل رمى النبي عليه السلام بفرث

BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r3.claim: The interrogative hamza expresses denial and the wāw coordinates this nominal clause with a like clause implied by the context.
BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r3.anchor: والهمزة للإنكار والنفي والواو لعطف الجملة الاسمية على مثلها

BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r4.claim: The implied rebuke asks whether believers are like the polytheists and like the person who remained spiritually dead.
BURSEVI:v3p74#3/r4.anchor: أنتم أيها المؤمنون مثل المشركين ومن كان ميتا

BURSEVI:v3p75/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p75/r1.claim: Giving life means granting life together with the powers of perception and movement.
BURSEVI:v3p75/r1.anchor: {فأحييناه} أعطيناه الحياة وما يتبعها من القوى

BURSEVI:v3p75/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p75/r2.claim: Along with that life, God gives the person a great light.
BURSEVI:v3p75/r2.anchor: {وجعلنا له} مع ذلك من الخارج {نورا} عظيما

BURSEVI:v3p75/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p75/r3.claim: The person moves among people by means of that light, safe from them.
BURSEVI:v3p75/r3.anchor: {يمشي به} أي : بسببه {فى الناس} أي : فيما بينهم آمنا من جهتهم

BURSEVI:v3p75/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p75/r4.claim: The phrase means his remarkable state; an omitted subject is understood before the predicate in the darknesses, and the clause ليس بخارج منها is circumstantial.
BURSEVI:v3p75/r4.anchor: {كمن مثله} أي صفته العجيبة {فى الظلمات} خبر مبتدأ محذوف

BURSEVI:v3p75/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p75/r5.claim: The living, illuminated person represents someone God guides from error, whose light of proofs lets him distinguish truth from falsehood and the sincere from the liar, like Ḥamza.
BURSEVI:v3p75/r5.anchor: الأولى تمثيل لمن هداه الله تعالى وأنقذه من الضلال

BURSEVI:v3p75/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p75/r6.claim: The person trapped in darkness represents one who remains fixed in misguidance and never leaves it, like Abū Jahl.
BURSEVI:v3p75/r6.anchor: والثانية تمثيل لمن بقي على الضلالة لا يفارقها أصلا كأبي جهل

BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r1.claim: The comparison means that, just as the believer's faith is made attractive, the disbelievers' deeds are made attractive to them.
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r1.anchor: {كذالك} أي : كما زين للمؤمن من إيمانه

BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r2.claim: The adornment may come from God by way of creation or from Satan by way of whispering.
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r2.anchor: {زين} أي : من جهة الله تعالى بطريق الخلق أو من جهة الشيطان بطريق الوسوسة

BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r3.claim: The disbelievers' persistent varieties of disbelief and sin are adorned for them, keeping them in darkness without faith or guidance.
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r3.anchor: ما استمروا على عمله من فنون الكفر والمعاصي

BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r4.speaker: أرباب الحقيقة
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r4.claim: The people of spiritual reality call following the lower self death and love of the Real life; ignorance is death and gnosis is life.
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r4.anchor: قال أرباب الحقيقة : الموت بهوى النفس والحياة بمحبة الحق

BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r5.speaker: أرباب الحقيقة
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r5.claim: Ordinary people live biologically yet remain buried in the darkness of metaphorical existence; the elect live by gnosis, which outlasts bodily life.
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r5.anchor: فأهل العموم حي بحياة البشرية لكنه كالميت في قبر قالبه

BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r6.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r6.claim: A Prophetic report says that the believer is alive in both abodes, supporting the distinction between bodily life and the life of gnosis.
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r6.anchor: وقوله عليه السلام : "المؤمن حي في الدارين"

BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r7.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r7.claim: Ḥāfiẓ's poem says that one whose heart is made alive by love does not die, expressing the lasting life of love.
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r7.anchor: قال الحافظ : هركز نميزد آنكه دلش زنده شد بعشق

BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r8.speaker: شاه كرمان
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r8.claim: The King of Kerman says the verse's signs are seclusion from people, calling to God, and continuous remembrance by tongue and heart.
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r8.anchor: وفي "التفسير الفارسي" : (شاه كرمان اين آيت برخواندكه

BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r9.claim: God alone is truly living without ever having been dead or dying; everything else was nonexistent and will die. In love's annihilation, creation is witnessed as dead.
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r9.anchor: واعلم : أن الحي الحقيقي الذي ما كان ميتا ولا يموت أبدا هو الله تعالى وما سواه فهو ميت

BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r10.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿArabī describes realization as progressively seeing creatures without independent acts, without life, and finally as identical with nonexistence.
BURSEVI:v3p75#2/r10.anchor: قال الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره الأطهر : من شهد الخلق لا فعل لهم فاز

DURR-FULL:v3p352/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r1.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the person who was dead and then given life as Umar ibn al-Khattab.
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه} قال: عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه

DURR-FULL:v3p352/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the person stranded in darkness as Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r2.anchor: كمن مثله في الظلمات} قال: أبو جهل بن هشام

DURR-FULL:v3p352/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r3.speaker: أبو سنان
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r3.claim: Abu Sinan reports that the verse was revealed concerning Umar ibn al-Khattab.
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r3.anchor: عن أبي سنان {أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه} قال: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب

DURR-FULL:v3p352/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r4.claim: Qatada says the believer has God's proof, the Book of God, by which he acts, takes guidance, and reaches his destination.
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس} قال: هذا المؤمن معه من الله بينة

DURR-FULL:v3p352/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r5.claim: Qatada compares the unbeliever to someone confused and stumbling in misguidance, unable to find an exit or way out.
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r5.anchor: كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها} قال: مثل الكافر في ضلالته متحير فيها متسكع فيها

DURR-FULL:v3p352/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the light as the Qur'an.
DURR-FULL:v3p352/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس} قال: القرآن

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r1.claim: He says the person who was dead was an unbeliever who had gone astray.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : أو من كان ميتا يعني كان كافرا ضالا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r2.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وأبو سنان
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r2.claim: These authorities are reported to give the same unbeliever-and-error interpretation.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r2.anchor: وروى عن مجاهد والسدى وابي سنان نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r3.claim: Through Abu Sinan, Dahhak identifies the verse's person as ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r3.anchor: عن أبي سنان عن الضحاك في قوله : أو من كان ميتا فاحييناه قال : عمر بن الخطاب

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r4.claim: He says the verse was revealed about ʿUmar: the Prophet prayed for Islam to be strengthened through Abu Jahl or ʿUmar; God guided and strengthened ʿUmar while leaving Abu Jahl in error.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم انه قال في قول الله : أو من كان ميتا فاحييناه فدعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r5.claim: He says the verse was revealed about ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة : اومن كان ميتا فاحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس قال : نزلت في عمار بن ياسر

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r6.claim: He glosses “We gave him life” as “We guided him.”
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : اومن كان ميتا فاحييناه يعني فهديناه

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r7.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وأبو سنان
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r7.claim: These authorities are reported to give the same guidance gloss.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r7.anchor: وروى عن مجاهد والسدى وابي سنان نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r8.claim: He identifies the light as the Qur'an, which a person believes and follows in practice.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس يعني بالنور : القران ، من صدق به وعمل به

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r9.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r9.claim: He describes the light as guidance by which God leads a polytheist to Islam; Mujahid is reported to give the same explanation.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1381/r9.anchor: عن عطية عن ابن عباس : قوله : أو من كان ميتا فاحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس قال : يقول : الهدى

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r1.claim: He identifies the light with Islam.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r1.anchor: عن السدى : قوله : وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس وهو الاسلام

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r2.claim: The believer has a clear proof from God by which he acts, receives guidance, and directs himself; that proof is God's Book.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r2.anchor: عن قتادة : قوله أو من كان ميتا فاحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس هذا المومن ، معه من الله

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r3.speaker: أبو سنان الشيباني
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r3.claim: He takes walking by the light as acting by it among people and says the verse was revealed about ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r3.anchor: عن أبي سنان الشيباني في قوله : وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس قال : يعمل به في الناس

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r4.claim: He explains the darknesses as unbelief and misguidance.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : كمن مثله في الظلمات يعني بالظلمات الكفر والضلالة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r5.claim: He says the person remains in misguidance forever; ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz is reported to say the same.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد : قوله : كمن مثله في الظلمات قال : في الضلالة ابدا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r6.claim: He identifies the one trapped in the darkness as Abu Jahl ibn Hisham; Ikrima, Zayd ibn Aslam, and Abu Sinan are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك : قوله : كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها قال : أبو جهل بن هشام

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r7.claim: He says the person in darkness does not know what will come or what will befall him.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r7.anchor: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم يقول : في قوله : كمن مثله في الظلمات قال : لا يدري ما ياتي وما يقع عليه

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r8.claim: The unbeliever is bewildered and stumbling in error, with no way out or opening from it.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1382/r8.anchor: عن قتادة : قوله : كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها قال : مثل الكافر في ضلالته ، متحير فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r1.claim: The interrogative clause is coordinated with 6:121; the earlier warning implies that the debate concerned religion, improving polytheism and condemning Islamic rules on carrion and non-God offerings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r1.anchor: الواو في قوله : { أو من كان ميتا } عاطفة لجملة الاستفهام على جملة : { وإن أطعتموهم إنكم لمشركون } ( الأنعام : 121 ) لتضمن قوله : { وإن أطعتموهم } أن المجادلة ، المذكورة من قبل ، مجادلة في الدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r2.claim: After warning Muslims about the satanic allies' arguments, the verse contrasts former polytheists who embraced Islam with those who remained polytheists, denying parity to show Islam's goodness and shirk's ugliness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r2.anchor: فلما حذر الله المسلمين من دسائس أولياء الشياطين ومجادلتهم بقوله : { وإن أطعتموهم إنكم لمشركون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r3.claim: The interrogative hamza rejects equality: the convert from shirk is like one brought from death and darkness into life, clear light, and a path among people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r3.anchor: والهمزة للاستفهام المستعمل في إنكار تماثل الحالتين : فالحالة الأولى : حالة الذين أسلموا بعد أن كانوا مشركين ، وهي المشبهة بحال من كان ميتا مودعا في ظلمات ، فصار حيا في نور واضح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r4.claim: The second case is the polytheist, like someone remaining in darkness without an exit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r4.anchor: والحالة الثانية : حالة المشرك وهي المشبهة بحالة من هو في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها ، لأنه في ظلمات .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r5.claim: The first ellipsis means either “is one who was dead equal?” or “the condition of one who was dead.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r5.anchor: وفي الكلام إيجاز حذفف ، في ثلاثة مواضع ، استغناء بالمذكور عن المحذوف : فقوله : { أو من كان ميتا } معناه : أحال من كان ميتا ، أو صفة من كان ميتا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r6.claim: The mention of light and walking implies the comparison case of someone dead in darkness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r6.anchor: وقوله : { وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس } يدل على أن المشبه به حال من كان ميتا في ظلمات .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r7.claim: The third ellipsis means “like one whose condition is like that of a dead person”; the comparison with the dead in the first case confirms that the omitted figure is dead.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r7.anchor: وقوله : كمن مثله في الظلمات تقديره : كمن مثله مثل ميت فما صدق ( من ) ميت بدليل مقابلته بميت في الحالة المشبهة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r8.claim: Mithl here means a condition or state.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r9.claim: Denying resemblance means denying equality, a clear indirect assertion that one state is better; the author illustrates this with 13:16 and 32:18.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r9.anchor: ونفي المشابهة هنا معناه نفي المساواة ، ونفي المساواة كناية عن تفضيل إحدى الحالتين على الأخرى تفضيلا لا يلتبس ، فذلك معنى نفي المشابهة كقوله : { قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير أم هل تستوي الظلمات والنور }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r10.claim: The kāf is a simile particle, and the comparison is negated through an interrogative of denial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p43/r10.anchor: والكاف في قوله : { كمن مثله في الظلمات } كاف التشبيه ، وهو تشبيه منفي بالاستفهام الإنكاري .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r1.claim: The clauses form two complete representations: a convert's condition resembles a dead person revived, while the persistent polytheist resembles a dead person still in a grave; together they deny likeness between the groups.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r1.anchor: والكلام جار على طريقة تمثيل حال من أسلم وتخلص من الشرك بحال من كان ميتا فأحيي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r2.claim: The paired clauses contain two composite comparisons, while the interrogative and kāf together deny that the convert and the one who remains in shirk are alike.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r2.anchor: فتضمنت جملة : { أو من كان ميتا } إلى آخرها تمثيل الحالة الأولى ، وجملة : { كمن مثله في الظلمات } الخ تمثيل الحالة الثانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r3.speaker: القطب الرازي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r3.claim: Al-Qutb al-Rāzī, in his commentary on al-Kashshāf, classifies the constructions as representational similes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r3.anchor: فنحا القطب الرازي في ( شرح الكشاف ) القبيل الأول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r4.speaker: التفتزاني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r4.claim: Al-Taftazānī classifies the constructions as representational metaphors.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers al-Taftazānī's analysis: these are representational metaphors, and the kāf refers to the denied similarity of the two clauses together, not to their internal state comparisons.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r5.anchor: والأظهر ما نحاه التفتزاني : أنهما استعارتان تمثيليتان ، وأما كاف التشبيه فهو متوجه إلى المشابهة المنفية في مجموع الجملتين لا إلى مشابهة الحالين بالحالين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r6.claim: The darkness is that of the grave, fitting the dead person and the literal sense of “in” and “exit.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r6.anchor: والمراد : ب { الظلمات } ظلمة القبر لمناسبته للميت ، وبقرينة ظاهر { في } من حقيقة الظرفية وظاهر حقيقة فعل الخروج .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r7.claim: Shirk makes a person useless and unable to distinguish truth from falsehood or seek salvation, like a dead person in darkness; Islam restores discernment, pursuit of good, and avoidance of corruption, like life and guiding light.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r7.anchor: فإن الشرك يحول دون التمييز بين الحق والباطل ، ويصرف صاحبه عن السعي إلى ما فيه خيره ونجاته ، وهو في ظلمة لو أفاق لم يعرف أين ينصرف ، فإذا هداه الله إلى الإسلام تغير حاله فصار يميز بين الحق والباطل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r8.claim: The image establishes the superiority of people with upright judgment over their opposites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p44/r8.anchor: وقد تبين بهذا التمثيل تفضيل أهل استقامة العقول على أضدادهم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r1.claim: The bāʾ in “walks by it” is causal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r1.anchor: والباء في قوله : { يمشي به } باء السببية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r2.claim: The explicit “people” belong to the compared scene as living members of human society; the implied people in the represented scene are the convert's fellow Muslims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r2.anchor: والناس المصرح به في الهيئة المشبه بها هم الأحياء الذين لا يخلو عنهم المجتمع الإنساني . والناس المقدر في الهيئة المشبهة هم رفقاء المسلم من المسلمين .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r3.claim: The composite image is complete enough to compare either the whole scene with the whole scene or each component with its counterpart, which is the highest form of representation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r3.anchor: وقد جاء المركب التمثيلي تاما صالحا لاعتبار تشبيه الهيئة بالهيئة ، ولاعتبار تشبيه كل جزء من أجزاء الهيئة المشبهة بجزء من أجزاء الهيئة المشبه بها ، كما قد علمته وذلك أعلى التمثيل .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r4.claim: The clause is circumstantial with respect to the pronoun governed by “likeness.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r4.anchor: وجملة : { ليس بخارج منها } حال من الضمير المجرور بإضافة ( مثل )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r5.claim: The person in shirk is immersed in darkness with no hope of finding light while remaining in that state.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r5.anchor: أي ظلمات لا يرجى للواقع فيها تنور بنور ما دام في حالة الإشراك .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r6.claim: The final clause is an explanatory resumption: the parable prompts the question why the polytheists stayed in error and failed to perceive the difference despite their intelligence and the proofs offered.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r6.anchor: وجملة : { كذلك زين للكافرين ما كانوا يعملون } استئناف بياني ، لأن التمثيل المذكور قبلها يثير في نفس السامع سؤالا ، أن يقول : كيف رضوا لأنفسهم البقاء في هذه الضلالات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r7.claim: Their persistence is explained by the astonishing embellishment of their deeds by the devils.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r7.anchor: وهو أن ما عملوه كان تزينه لهم الشياطين ، هذا التزيين العجيب ، الذي لو أراد أحد تقريبه لم يجد ضلالا مزينا أوضح منه وأعجب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r8.claim: “In that way” points back to the astonishing, cunning embellishment denoted by the verb, as in the earlier wording in 2:143.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r8.anchor: واسم الإشارة في قوله : { كذلك زين للكافرين } مشار به إلى التزيين المأخوذ من فعل { زين } أي مثل ذلك التزيين للكافرين العجيب كيدا ودقة زين لهؤلاء الكافرين أعمالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r9.claim: The verb is passive and its agent omitted because the focus is the occurrence of embellishment, not identifying its agent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r9.anchor: وحذف فاعل التزيين فبني الفعل للمجهول : لأن المقصود وقوع التزيين لا معرفة من أوقعه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r10.claim: The agents are their devils and allies: human devils directly embellish, while jinn devils prompt and adorn the deeds, as in 6:137.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r10.anchor: والمزين شياطينهم وأولياؤهم ، كقوله : وكذلك زين لكثير من المشركين قتل أولادهم شركاؤهم } ( الأنعام : 137 ) ، ولأن الشياطين من الإنس هم المباشرون للتزيين ، وشياطين الجن هم المسولون المزينون .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r11.claim: “The disbelievers” refers here to the polytheists discussed in the preceding verses through 6:121.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p45/r11.anchor: والمراد بالكافرين المشركون الذين الكلام عليهم في الآيات السابقة إلى قوله : { وإن الشياطين ليوحون إلى أوليائهم ليجادلوكم } ( الأنعام : 121 ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p46/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p46/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p46/r1.claim: The conjunction connects this clause to 6:122 as another explanatory resumption, giving a further reason the polytheists persist: their leaders scheme against the Messenger and divert ordinary people from his call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p46/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة : { كذلك زين للكافرين ما كانوا يعملون } ( الأنعام : 122 ) فلها حكم الاستئناف البياني ، لبيان سبب آخر من أسباب استمرار المشركين على ضلالهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r1.claim: The comparison follows believers ordered to leave outward and inward sins and unbelievers led astray by desires.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r1.anchor: تقدم في هذه الآية السالفة ذكر قوم مؤمنين أمروا بترك الإثم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and others take believers after unbelief as dead people God revived.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r2.anchor: هذا معنى قول ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r3.claim: Unbelievers' bewilderment resembles people wandering in darkness with no way out.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r3.anchor: وشبه الكافرين وحيرة جهلهم بقوم في ظلمات يترددون فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r4.claim: The majority read aw-man with fatḥa on wāw: interrogative alif plus conjunction wāw, and man is a relative pronoun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «أو من» بفتح الواو فهي ألف استفهام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r5.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r5.claim: Ṭalḥa b. Muṣarrif reads afaman with fāʾ, close in meaning to the wāw reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف: «أفمن» بالفاء، والمعنى قريب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r6.claim: The fāʾ in fa-aḥyaynāhu is conjunctive.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r7.claim: The light most plausibly means faith, by which the believer acts and speaks among people; Abu ʿAlī allows the light of Judgment Day.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r7.anchor: ونورا أمكن ما يعنى به الإيمان ويمشي به يراد به جميع التصرف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r8.claim: Fī al-nās attaches to yamshī but can attach to kāna maytan; kaman mathaluhu equals kaman huwa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r8.anchor: وفي الناس متعلق ب يمشي، ويصح أن يتعلق ب كان ميتا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r9.claim: The ka may attach to an implied ‘as We revived believers,’ or to kaman mathaluhu, making the compared condition itself adornment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r9.anchor: والكاف في قوله كذلك زين متعلقة بمحذوف يدل ظاهر الكلام عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r10.speaker: نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r10.claim: Nāfiʿ alone reads mayyitan with kasra and doubled yāʾ; others use a still yāʾ. Abu ʿAlī says the forms are equivalent and the deleted yāʾ is the second, from wāw.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r10.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده «ميتا» بكسر الياء وشدها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r11.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r11.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the revived believer as ʿUmar; al-Mahdawī reports another view identifying Ḥamza.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r11.anchor: فقال الضحاك: المؤمن الذي كان ميتا فأحيي عمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r12.speaker: عكرمة والزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r12.claim: ʿIkrima identifies ʿAmmār b. Yāsir; al-Zajjāj says it refers to the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p340#3/r12.anchor: وحكى المهدوي عن بعضهم أنه حمزة بن عبد المطلب، وقال عكرمة:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p341/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p341/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p341/r1.claim: The commentators agree the one in darkness is Abu Jahl; the comparison extends to his peers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p341/r1.anchor: واتفقوا على أن الذي في الظلمات أبو جهل بن هشام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r1.claim: One occasion report identifies the dead person as Hamza and Abu Jahl: after Abu Jahl threw filth at the Prophet, the newly converted Hamza struck him with a bow, denounced idolatry, and declared faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r1.anchor: فنزلت هذه الآية هذا قول ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r2.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس، عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r2.claim: A second occasion report says the verse concerns ʿAmmar b. Yasir and Abu Jahl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r2.anchor: والثاني أنها نزلت في عمار بن ياسر وأبي جهل رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم، الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r3.claim: A third occasion report identifies ʿUmar b. al-Khattab and Abu Jahl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r3.anchor: والثالث في عمر بن الخطاب وأبي جهل قاله زيد بن أسلم والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r4.claim: A fourth occasion report identifies the Prophet and Abu Jahl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r4.anchor: والرابع في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وابي جهل قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r5.speaker: الحسن وآخرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r5.claim: A fifth view says the verse is general, applying to every believer and disbeliever.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r5.anchor: والخامس أنها عامة في كل مؤمن وكافر قاله الحسن في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r6.claim: One interpretation of having been dead is having been astray, then guided.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r6.anchor: أحدهما كان ضالا فهديناه قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r7.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r7.claim: Another interpretation is having been ignorant, then taught.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r7.anchor: والثاني كان جاهلا فعلمناه قاله الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r8.speaker: نافع، أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r8.claim: Nafiʿ reads mayyitan with a doubled ya; Abu ʿUbayd says the lightened and doubled forms have the same meaning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r8.anchor: وقرأ نافع ميتا بالتشديد قال أبو عبيدة الميتة مخففة من ميتة والمعنى واحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r9.claim: One view identifies the light as guidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r9.anchor: أحدها أنه الهدى قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r10.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r10.claim: A second view identifies the light as the Qurʾan.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r11.claim: A third view identifies the light as knowledge.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r11.anchor: والثالث العلم وفي قوله ﴿ يمشي به في الناس ﴾ ثلاثة أقوال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r12.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r12.claim: One interpretation says that the person is guided by the light among people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r12.anchor: أحدها يهتدي به في الناس قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r13.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r13.claim: Another interpretation is that he walks by it among people toward Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r13.anchor: والثاني يمشي به بين الناس إلى الجنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r14.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r14.claim: A third says he spreads his religion among people, becoming like one who walks.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p116/r14.anchor: والثالث ينشر به دينه في الناس فيصير كالماشي ذكرهما الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r1.claim: One syntactic explanation treats mathal as an extra particle, yielding the sense: like someone who is in darkness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r1.anchor: المثل صلة والمعنى كمن هو في الظلمات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r2.claim: An alternative construal means: like someone whose likeness, if compared with something, would be that of a person in darkness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r2.anchor: وقيل المعنى كمن لو شبه بشيء كان شبيهه من في الظلمات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r3.claim: The darknesses here refer to disbelief.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r4.claim: As the person in darkness cannot escape it, so disbelievers have had their deeds made attractive: idolatry and sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p117/r4.anchor: أي كما بقي هذا في ظلماته لا يتخلص منها كذلك زين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r1.claim: The dead person represents someone lost, bewildered, and doomed in misguidance; God revives his heart with faith, guides him, and enables him to follow His messengers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r1.anchor: فأحياه الله، أي: أحيا قلبه بالإيمان، وهداه له ووفقه لاتباع رسله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r2.speaker: العوفي وابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r2.claim: Al-ʿAwfi and Ibn Abi Talha report Ibn ʿAbbas’s explanation that the light is the Qurʾan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r2.anchor: والنور هو: القرآن، كما رواه العوفي وابن أبي طلحة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the light is Islam; Ibn Kathir considers this and the Qurʾan interpretation both correct.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r4.claim: The darknesses are ignorance, divergent desires, and forms of misguidance; the person cannot find an exit or escape from them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r4.anchor: لا يهتدي إلى منفذ، ولا مخلص

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r5.claim: A report in Ahmad’s Musnad says God created creation in darkness, then sprinkled them with His light; whoever received it was guided, and whoever missed it went astray.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r5.anchor: إن الله خلق خلقه في ظلمة ثم رش عليهم من نوره فمن أصابه ذلك النور اهتدى ومن أخطأه ضل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r6.claim: The light-and-darkness contrast echoes 2:257, 67:22, 11:24, and 35:19–23; its pairing also recalls the opening of this sūra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r6.anchor: ووجه المناسبة في ضرب المثلين هاهنا بالنور والظلمات، ما (7) تقدم في أول السورة:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r7.claim: The contrast between the guided and unguided is also compared with one walking face-down versus upright and with blind/deaf versus seeing/hearing people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r7.anchor: أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه أهدى أمن يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r8.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r8.claim: Some identify the person brought to life as ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r8.anchor: فقيل: عمر بن الخطاب هو الذي كان ميتا فأحياه الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r9.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r9.claim: Another reported identification makes ʿAmmar ibn Yasir the person brought to life and given light.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r10.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r10.claim: Some identify the one trapped in darkness as Abu Jahl, ʿAmr ibn Hisham.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r10.anchor: وأما الذي في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها: أبو جهل عمرو بن هشام، لعنه الله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects limiting the parable to named individuals: it applies generally to every believer and unbeliever.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p330/r11.anchor: والصحيح أن الآية عامة، يدخل فيها كل مؤمن وكافر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p331/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
