IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p331/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p331/r1.claim: God made the disbelievers’ ignorance and misguidance seem good to them by His decree and profound wisdom; there is no deity or lord besides Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p331/r1.anchor: حسنا لهم ما هم فيه من الجهالة والضلالة، قدرا من الله وحكمة بالغة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r1.claim: The guided person, raised from misguidance and given certainty to distinguish truth from falsehood, resembles someone revived and given light to move among people and discern them; the misguided remain lost in darkness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r1.anchor: مثل الذي هداه الله بعد الضلالة ومنحه التوفيق لليقين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r2.claim: The construction means someone whose description is that he is in darkness and cannot leave it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r2.anchor: هو في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r3.claim: The author compares this construction to the description of Paradise as having rivers: the following clause supplies the likeness’s attribute.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r3.anchor: أي صفتها هذه ، وهي قوله : { فيها أنهار }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r4.claim: The deeds may have been made attractive to disbelievers by Satan.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r5.claim: Alternatively, God made their deeds attractive, as in the verse saying that We adorned their deeds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p59/r5.anchor: أو الله عز وعلا على قوله :

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r1.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r1.claim: Ibn Bahr says the person was dead as a sperm drop and was brought to life by the breathing of the spirit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r1.anchor: كان ميتا حين كان نطفة فأحييناه بنفخ الروح [ فيه ] , حكاه ابن بحر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r2.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r2.claim: Ibn Isa says the person was dead through unbelief and was brought to life by guidance to faith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r2.anchor: كان ميتا بالكفر فأحييناه بالهداية إلى الإيمان , حكاه ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r3.claim: A third view says the person was dead through ignorance and was brought to life through knowledge and action; verses from a Basran poet support it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r3.anchor: كان ميتا بالجهل فأحييناه بالعمل , أنشدني بعض أهل العلم ما يدل على صحة هذا التأويل لبعض شعراء البصرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r4.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r4.claim: Hasan identifies the light as the Qur'an.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r5.claim: Another view identifies the light as knowledge that guides toward right conduct.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r5.anchor: أنه العلم الذي يهدي إلى الرشد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r6.claim: A third view identifies the light as the beauty of faith.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r7.claim: One reading means that the believer spreads the mention of his religion among people in this world, as if walking.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r7.anchor: ينشر به ذكر دينه بين الناس في الدنيا حتى يصير كالماشي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r8.claim: Alternatively, he walks guided among people toward Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r8.anchor: يهتدي به بين الناس إلى الجنة فيكون هو الماشي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r11.claim: Ignorance is likened to darkness because the ignorant person is bewildered and headed toward ruin like someone walking in darkness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r11.anchor: لأن صاحبه في حيرة تفضي به إلى الهلكة كحيرة الماشي في الظلمة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r12.speaker: الحسن، غيره من أهل العلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r12.claim: One view treats the comparison as general, applying to every believer and disbeliever.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r12.anchor: أنها على العموم في كل مؤمن وكافر , قاله الحسن وغيره من أهل العلم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r13.speaker: الضحاك، مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r13.claim: A particularized view identifies the believer as Umar and the disbeliever as Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r13.anchor: أن المؤمن عمر بن الخطاب , والكافر أبو جهل , قاله الضحاك . ومقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r14.speaker: عكرمة، الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r14.claim: Another particularized view identifies the believer as Ammar ibn Yasir and the disbeliever as Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p162/r14.anchor: أن المؤمن عمار بن ياسر , والكافر أبو جهل , قاله عكرمة , والكلبي .

MUQATIL:6:122-124/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r1.claim: Being dead and then given life means being astray and then guided; the verse was revealed concerning the Prophet.
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r1.anchor: { أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه } ، يعنى أو من كان ضالا فهديناه، نزلت فى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم،

MUQATIL:6:122-124/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r2.claim: The light given to him is faith, by which he is guided among people.
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r2.anchor: { وجعلنا له نورا } ، يعنى إيمانا { يمشي به } ، يعنى يهتدى به { في الناس } ،

MUQATIL:6:122-124/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r3.claim: The person in darkness is Abū Jahl, whose likeness is in polytheism and who is not guided.
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r3.anchor: { كمن مثله في الظلمات } ، يعنى كشبه من هو فى الشرك، يعنى أبا جهل، { ليس بخارج منها }

MUQATIL:6:122-124/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r4.claim: Abū Jahl is bewildered in polytheism, unable to find a way out, so he and the guided person are not alike.
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r4.anchor: يعنى من الشرك، يعنى ليس بمهتد، هو فهيا متحير لا يجد منفذا، ليسا بسواء،

MUQATIL:6:122-124/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r5.claim: The disbelievers whose deeds are made attractive are the polytheists, specifically Abū Jahl.
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r5.anchor: { كذلك } ، يعنى هكذا، { زين للكافرين } ، يعنى للمشركين، { ما كانوا يعملون } [آية: 122]، يعنى أبا جهل،

MUQATIL:6:122-124/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r6.speaker: أبو جهل
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r6.claim: Abū Jahl said Banū ʿAbd Manāf had matched his clan in prestige and now claimed a prophet; he swore they would never believe or follow unless they too received revelation.
MUQATIL:6:122-124/r6.anchor: يعنى أبا جهل، وذلك أنه قال: زحمتنا بنو عبد مناف فى الشرف، حتى إذا صرنا كفرسى رهان،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r1.claim: Dead means an unbeliever whom God guided; faith gives life to hearts.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r1.anchor: أى كافرا فهديناه لأن الإيمان حيات القلوب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r2.speaker: مدنى
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r2.claim: The Medinan reader has a variant pronunciation of mayyitan.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r2.anchor: ميتا مدنى ﴿ وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r3.claim: The light is certainty, by which the guided person walks among people.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r4.claim: The disbeliever stumbles in darkness, unable to leave or escape it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r4.anchor: ﴿ فى الظلمات ﴾ أى خابط فيها ﴿ ليس بخارج منها ﴾ لا يفارقها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r5.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r5.claim: One view identifies the two figures as Hamza and Abū Jahl.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r5.anchor: قيل المراد بهما حمزة و أبو جهل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r6.claim: The stronger reading is general: every person God guides is like the revived, illuminated believer, and every person He leads astray like the trapped disbeliever.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r6.anchor: والأصح أن الآية عامة لكل من هداه الله ولكل من أضله الله فبين أن مثل المهتدى مثل الميت الذى أحيى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r7.claim: As God adorns faith for believers, He adorns the disbelievers' deeds for them, as in 6:108.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p343#3/r7.anchor: ﴿ زين للكافرين ﴾ بتزيين الله تعالى كقوله زينا لهم أعمالهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r1.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r1.claim: The majority read the waw in the opening with fatḥa, preceded by the interrogative hamza.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r1.anchor: قرأ الجمهور بفتح الواو، دخلت عليها همزة الاستفهام.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r2.speaker: المسيبي عن نافع بن أبي نعيم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r2.claim: Al-Musayyibi transmits from Nafi a reading with the waw in أو من quiescent; al-Nahhas says the construction can follow the meaning, joining the question about seeking a judge to an invitation to reflect on the revived person.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r2.anchor: وروى المسيبي عن نافع بن أبي نعيم «أو من كان» بإسكان الواو. قال النحاس: يجوز أن يكون محمولا على المعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r3.speaker: ابن بحر
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r3.claim: Ibn Bahr says the person was dead as a sperm drop and was given life when the spirit was breathed into him.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r3.anchor: قيل: معناه كان ميتا حين كان نطفة فأحييناه بنفخ الروح فيه حكاه ابن بحر.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reads death as unbelief and revival as guidance, and says the verse was revealed about Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Abu Jahl.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أو من كان كافرا فهديناه. نزلت في حمزة بن عبد المطلب وأبي جهل.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Suddi identify the one given life as Umar and the person in darkness as Abu Jahl.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r5.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم والسدي: «فأحييناه» عمر رضي الله عنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers a general reading: the verse concerns every believer and unbeliever.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r6.anchor: والصحيح أنها عامة في كل مؤمن وكافر.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r7.claim: Another interpretation takes death as ignorance and revival as knowledge; a Basran poet's lines support this figurative sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r7.anchor: وقيل: كان ميتا بالجهل فأحييناه بالعلم. وأنشد بعض أهل العلم ما يدل على صحة هذا التأويل لبعض شعراء البصرة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r8.claim: The light means guidance and faith.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r9.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the light as the Qur'an.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r9.anchor: والنور عبارة عن الهدى والإيمان. وقال الحسن: القرآن.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r10.claim: Another interpretation identifies the light as wisdom.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r11.claim: Another interpretation identifies this light with the light mentioned in the two verses of Surat al-Hadid.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r11.anchor: وقيل: هو النور المذكور في قوله: يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r12.claim: The phrase means that the person walks among people by means of the light.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r12.anchor: يمشي به } أي بالنور { في الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r13.claim: In كمن مثله في الظلمات, mithl is extra, as in expressions meaning I honor you and in the cited examples from al-Maida and al-Shura.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r13.anchor: فمثل زائدة. تقول: أنا أكرم مثلك أي أكرمك. ومثله

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r14.claim: An alternative parses it as one whose likeness is the likeness of someone in darkness; mithl and mathal have the same meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r14.anchor: وقيل: المعنى كمن مثله مثل من هو في الظلمات. والمثل والمثل واحد.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r15.claim: Satan made idol worship attractive to unbelievers and deluded them into thinking they were better than Muslims.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:122/r15.anchor: أي زين لهم الشيطان عبادة الأصنام، وأوهمهم أنهم أفضل من المسلمين.

RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r1.claim: After saying that idolaters dispute with believers about religion, the passage gives a parable contrasting guided believers with lost unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r1.anchor: لما ذكر في الآية الأولى أن المشركين يجادلون المؤمنين في دين الله ذكر مثلا

RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r2.claim: The guided believer is like someone made alive and given light to find his interests; the unbeliever remains immersed in darkness, endlessly bewildered.
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r2.anchor: فبين أن المؤمن المهتدي بمنزلة من كان ميتا ، فجعل حيا بعد ذلك وأعطى نورا يهتدى به في مصالحه

RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r3.claim: Razi's school says God is the one who adorns unbelievers' deeds: action depends on a motivating judgment of greater benefit, and God creates that motive.
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r3.anchor: فقال أصحابنا : ذلك المزين هو الله تعالى ، ودليله ما سبق ذكره من أن الفعل يتوقف على حصول الداعي

RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r4.speaker: المعتزلة والحسن
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r4.claim: The Mu'tazila say Satan adorns the deeds; they quote al-Hasan as saying that the one who adorned them was Satan.
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r4.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة : ذلك المزين هو الشيطان ، وحكوا عن الحسن أنه قال : زينه لهم والله الشيطان

RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r5.claim: Razi rejects Satan as the sole adornment: his prior proof points to God; assigning Satan's unbelief to another satan causes an infinite regress; and 6:108 and 6:123 explicitly attribute adornment or placement of criminals to God.
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r5.anchor: واعلم أن هذا في غاية الضعف لوجوه : الأول : الدليل القاطع

RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r6.speaker: نافع
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r6.claim: Nafiʿ reads ميتا with a doubled ya; the other readers lighten it, and language scholars say both forms have the same meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v13p139#2/r6.anchor: قرأ نافع { ميتا } مشددا ، والباقون مخففا

RAZI-FULL:v13p140/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p140/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p140/r1.claim: Other verses call unbelievers dead and contrast life with death (16:21, 36:70, 27:80, 35:19, 35:22); Razi says disbelief is death because ignorance causes perplexity and stillness, while guidance is knowledge and insight leading to salvation.
RAZI-FULL:v13p140/r1.anchor: فلما جعل الكفر موتا والكافر ميتا ، جعل الهدى حياة والمهتدي حيا ، وإنما جعل الكفر موتا لأنه جهل

RAZI-FULL:v13p140/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p140/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p140/r2.claim: Because جعلنا له نورا is coordinated with فأحييناه, the light must signify something distinct from the life.
RAZI-FULL:v13p140/r2.anchor: عطف على قوله { فأحييناه } فوجب أن يكون هذا النور مغايرا

RAZI-FULL:v13p140/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p140/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p140/r3.claim: Razi models knowledge in four soul-stages: initial capacity to receive knowledge, primary universal axioms, acquired theoretical knowledge available for recall, and sacred insights present and illuminating the spirit; the first stage is called death.
RAZI-FULL:v13p140/r3.anchor: الأرواح البشرية لها أربع مراتب في المعرفة

RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r1.claim: In Razi's four-stage model, primary universal knowledge is life, reasoning from axioms to theory is the light, and actively present sacred insights are walking by it; this completes the soul's happiness.
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r1.anchor: المرتبة الثانية : وهي أن تحصل العلوم البديهية الكلية فيه

RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r2.claim: A further reading calls life the soul's readiness and light the arrival of revelation: as sight needs a sound sense and sunlight, spiritual vision needs sound reason and revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r2.anchor: الحياة عبارة عن الاستعداد القائم بجوهر الروح ، والنور عبارة عن إيصال نور الوحي

RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r3.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r3.claim: Other commentators identify the light as the Quran, the light of religion, or the light of wisdom; Razi says these are close but prefers his earlier account.
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون : المراد بهذا النور ، القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r4.claim: A person continually immersed in ignorance and blameworthy traits makes those darknesses seem innate and hard to remove; darkness also leaves him confused, afraid and helpless.
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r4.anchor: إذا دام كون الكافر في ظلمات الجهل والأخلاق الذميمة صارت تلك الظلمات كالصفة الذاتية اللازمة له

RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerns Hamza and Abu Jahl: after Abu Jahl threw dung at Muhammad, Hamza returned from hunting, struck Abu Jahl with his bow, condemned idol worship and declared faith; Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v13p141/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس : إن أبا جهل رمى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بفرث

RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r1.claim: Muqatil says the verse concerns Muhammad and Abu Jahl, who said he would not believe unless revelation came to him as it came to the Prophet; Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل : نزلت هذه الآية في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبي جهل

RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة والكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r2.claim: Ikrima and al-Kalbi say the verse was revealed about Ammar ibn Yasir and Abu Jahl; Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r2.anchor: قال عكرمة والكلبي : نزلت في عمار بن ياسر وأبي جهل

RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse was revealed about Umar ibn al-Khattab and Abu Jahl; Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r3.anchor: قال الضحاك : نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب وأبي جهل

RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r4.claim: Razi prefers a general application to every believer and unbeliever because the meaning fits everyone; since the sura descended all at once, particular occasions are difficult to assert without a prophetic statement specifying an individual.
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r4.anchor: إن هذه الآية عامة في حق جميع المؤمنين والكافرين ، وهذا هو الحق

RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r5.claim: Razi argues that faith and disbelief come from God: life and light mean knowledge and guidance, motives are divinely created, and a person seeking knowledge but getting ignorance must have had the opposite produced in him; blaming error on mistaking it for knowledge regresses to prior ignorance unless some is created externally.
RAZI-FULL:v13p141#2/r5.anchor: هذه الآية من أقوى الدلائل أيضا على أن الكفر والإيمان من الله تعالى

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r1.claim: The life-giving is a metaphor for spiritual awakening; the light is religious guidance, perhaps the Quran specifically.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r1.anchor: God’s giving “life” to one who was dead is a metaphor for spiritual awakening

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r2.claim: The light by which one walks among people is a source of religious guidance, perhaps the Quran itself.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r2.anchor: a source of religious guidance, or perhaps the Quran specifically

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r3.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī reads the revived person as one whose soul God prepared to receive revelation’s spiritual guidance.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r3.anchor: Al-Rāzī interprets the one to whom God “gives life” as a reference to a person whose soul God has prepared

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r4.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī identifies the light by which one walks among people with revelation itself.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r4.anchor: Al-Rāzī interprets the one to whom God “gives life” as a reference to a person whose soul God has prepared to receive the spiritual guidance of revelation, and the light by which to walk among mankind as revelation itself

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r5.claim: Light commonly symbolizes spiritual guidance and revelation in this life, while the righteous also have guiding light in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r5.anchor: Light is a common Quranic symbol for spiritual guidance and revelation, usually in this life

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r6.claim: The image of walking among people by light is also used for God-given guidance in 57:28.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r6.anchor: For the idea of light as a symbol for the means by which one might walk among mankind—that is, with guidance in the world—see 57:28

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r7.claim: God and His messengers are elsewhere said to bring people out of darkness into light.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r7.anchor: where God or His messengers are said to bring people out of darkness into light

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r8.claim: The commentary refers readers to its discussions of light and darkness in 6:1 and 24:35.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r8.anchor: For a fuller discussion of the meaning of light and darkness (lit.“darknesses”), see 6:1c; 24:35c

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r9.claim: The comparison is best understood generally as one between believers and disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r9.anchor: the verse is best understood as a metaphorical comparison between believers and disbelievers generally

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r10.speaker: one report
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r10.claim: One report connects the revelation to Ḥamzah embracing Islam after Abū Jahl insulted the Prophet: the spiritually revived Ḥamzah is unlike Abū Jahl in darkness.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r10.anchor: According to one report, after Abū Jahl insulted the Prophet, the powerful and respected Ḥamzah came to the defense of his nephew and openly embraced Islam

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r11.speaker: other reports
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r11.claim: Other reports identify the person given life and light as the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r11.anchor: Other reports consider the one who is given a light by which to walk among mankind a reference to the Prophet himself

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r12.speaker: reports (R, Ṭ, Ṭs)
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r12.claim: Other reports identify the person given life and light as ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r12.anchor: or to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who had initially opposed the message brought by the Prophet, but converted in Makkah

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r13.speaker: reports (R, Ṭ, Ṭs)
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r13.claim: Other reports identify the person given life and light as ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, an early Companion and supporter of ʿAlī.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r13.anchor: or to ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, an early Companion who later become a close supporter of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib after the Prophet’s death

STUDYQURAN:6:122/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r14.claim: The Quran repeatedly says disbelievers’ deeds are made fair-seeming; this sūrah discusses it in verses 43, 108, and 137.
STUDYQURAN:6:122/r14.anchor: That the actions of the disbelievers are made to seem fair unto them is found in several places in the Quran

SULAMI:v1p213#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r1.speaker: شاه الكرماني
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r1.claim: Three signs of spiritual life are intimacy replacing loneliness, fullness of the Real through constant remembrance, and awe born of pure watchfulness.
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r1.anchor: قال شاه الكرماني : علامة الحياة ثلاثة : وجدان الأنس بفقدان الوحشة ، والإمتلاء من الحق بإدمان التذكرة

SULAMI:v1p213#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r2.claim: God revives the one dead to Him through Himself, making him a guide whose light directs strangers and restores the lost; the contrasting person follows desire in darkness without nearness or divine companionship.
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r2.anchor: وقال جعفر في قوله : ^ ( أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه ) ^ قال : ميتا عنا فأحييناه بنا ، وجعلناه إماما

SULAMI:v1p213#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r3.claim: One dies through the self's life and the heart's death; God revives him by extinguishing the self and enlivening the heart, guiding him with lights of nearness so he sees and turns only to God.
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أو من كان ميتا بحياة نفسه وموت قلبه ، فأحييناه بإماتة نفسه وحياة قلبه

SULAMI:v1p213#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r4.speaker: شاه
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r4.claim: A heart's light is shown by seeing worldly life as passing, preparing for death as one's term approaches, and shedding tears at mention of the afterlife.
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r4.anchor: وقال شاه : علامة النور في القلب النظر إلى الدنيا بعين الزوال وتقرب الأجل بإبطال الأمل استعدادا للموت

SULAMI:v1p213#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r5.speaker: أبو محمد الجريري
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r5.claim: A servant whom God revives with His lights never dies, while one whom He leaves to abandonment never truly lives.
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو محمد الجريري : في قوله : ^ ( أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه ) ^ قال : إذا أحيا الله عبدا بأنواره لا تموت أبدا ، وإذا أماته بخذلانه

SULAMI:v1p213#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r6.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r6.claim: One dead through reliance on acts of obedience is revived by the light of supplication and apology.
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r6.anchor: وقال جعفر : أو من كان ميتا بالاعتماد على الطاعات ، فأحييناه : فجعلنا له نور التضرع

SULAMI:v1p213#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r7.claim: Seeing one's own actions is a kind of death; life comes through seeing one's neediness.
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ميتا برؤية الأفعال فأحييناه برؤية الافتقار

SULAMI:v1p213#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r8.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r8.claim: God gives His friends life through the light of awakening just as He gives bodies life through spirits.
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r8.anchor: وقال القاسم : أحيا أولياءه بنور الانتباه ، كما أحيا الأجساد بالأرواح

SULAMI:v1p213#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r9.speaker: القناء
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r9.claim: This is the life of gnosis rather than bodily life: the dead is absent in annihilation from invocations, then revived by dying to perception of us and living in us.
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r9.anchor: قال القناء : هذه حياة المعرفة لا حياة البشرية ، وقال : ميت لا ذكر له في الفناء عن الأذكار

SULAMI:v1p213#2/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r10.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r10.claim: Ignorance is death, while knowledge is life.
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r10.anchor: وقال سهل : من كان ميتا بالجهل فاحييناه بالعلم

SULAMI:v1p213#2/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r11.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r11.claim: Severance from God is death; He gives life through connection to Him and its light, unlike one left in the darkness of separation.
SULAMI:v1p213#2/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : أو من كان ميتا بالانقطاع عنه ، فأحييناه بالاتصال بنا وجعلنا له نورا اتصالا

TABATABAI:6:122/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122/r1.claim: At the plain level, the verse compares believer and unbeliever: before divine guidance a person is like the dead, while accepted faith revives and gives a light that distinguishes good from evil and benefit from harm.
TABATABAI:6:122/r1.anchor: فالإنسان قبل أن يمسه الهدى الإلهي كالميت المحروم من نعمة الحياة الذي لا حس له ولا حركة

TABATABAI:6:122/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122/r2.claim: The unbeliever resembles someone trapped without escape in death’s darkness and in ignorance about distinguishing good from evil and benefit from harm.
TABATABAI:6:122/r2.anchor: ظلمة الموت وما بعد ذلك من ظلمات الجهل في مرحلة تمييز الخير من الشر

TABATABAI:6:122/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122/r3.claim: For ordinary hearers, death represents misguidance, life faith or guidance, revival guidance to faith, light insight into good deeds, and darkness ignorance; the comparison uses familiar animal life as its frame.
TABATABAI:6:122/r3.anchor: ففي الكلام استعارة الموت للضلال واستعارة الحياة للإيمان أو الاهتداء والإحياء للهداية إلى الإيمان والنور للتبصر بالأعمال الصالحة

TABATABAI:6:122/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122/r4.claim: Verse 6:36 parallels the contrast between those who hear and the dead whom God will raise.
TABATABAI:6:122/r4.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية في معناها بوجه قوله تعالى إنما يستجيب الذين يسمعون والموتى يبعثهم الله الأنعام 36

TABATABAI:6:122/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122/r5.claim: Verse 16:97 similarly promises a good life to a believing man or woman who does righteous deeds.
TABATABAI:6:122/r5.anchor: وقال تعالى من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياة طيبة النحل 97

TABATABAI:6:122/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122/r6.claim: On a deeper Qurʾānic reading, the divinely guided person has an everlasting life beyond worldly death, protected by God, free of fatigue and hardship, immersed in divine love, secure and endlessly happy.
TABATABAI:6:122/r6.anchor: فإن الله سبحانه ينسب للإنسان الإلهي في كلامه حياة خالدة أبدية لا تنقطع بالموت الدنيوي

TABATABAI:6:122/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122/r7.claim: Because of this higher life, the believer sees, hears, understands, and wills what others do not; inward awareness and volition exceed theirs even when outward actions look alike.
TABATABAI:6:122/r7.anchor: ومن كان هذا شأنه فإنه يرى ما لا يراه الناس، ويسمع ما لا يسمعونه، ويعقل ما لا يعقلونه

TABATABAI:6:122#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r1.claim: Like human life surpasses animal life, the believer endowed with knowledge, faith, certainty, and devotion has a higher life, perception, and will than ordinary human life.
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r1.anchor: فلنقض في الإنسان الذي أوتي العلم والإيمان واستقر في دار الإيقان

TABATABAI:6:122#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r2.claim: The promise of a good life in 16:97 shows that believers possess a life that is good in its own nature and exceeds life in the unqualified sense.
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r2.anchor: فلهم الحياة لكنها بطبعها طيبة وراء مطلق الحياة

TABATABAI:6:122#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r3.claim: Disbelievers have counterparts of believers' hearts, eyes, and ears, but lack their perfected effects, evidence of a real difference in spiritual life.
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r3.anchor: يثبت لهم أمثال القلوب والأعين والأذان التي في المؤمنين لكنه ينفي كمال آثارها

TABATABAI:6:122#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r4.claim: The statement that God supports believers with a spirit from Him further shows their distinctive spiritual life is real.
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r4.anchor: حتى أثبت لهم روحا خاصا بهم فقال أولئك كتب في قلوبهم الإيمان وأيدهم بروح منه

TABATABAI:6:122#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r5.claim: The believer's life and light are actual realities, not merely figurative expressions; God's special believers have a stronger claim to the name life than ordinary people.
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r5.anchor: أن للحياة وكذا للنور حقيقة في المؤمن واقعية وليس الكلام جاريا على ذاك التجوز

TABATABAI:6:122#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r6.claim: The dead person is one inwardly astray or an unbeliever before faith; God revives him through faith or guidance, which have the same sense here.
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r6.anchor: أي ضالا من حيث نفسه أو ضالا كافرا قبل أن يؤمن بربه

TABATABAI:6:122#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r7.claim: The light given to the believer is knowledge that grows out of faith.
TABATABAI:6:122#2/r7.anchor: وجعلنا له نورا أي علما متولدا من إيمانه

TABATABAI:6:122#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r1.claim: A report transmitted by both Muslim groups says that whoever acts on what he knows is granted knowledge of what he did not know, or God teaches him what he did not know.
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r1.anchor: من عمل بما علم رزقه الله علم ما لم يعلم أو علمه الله ما لم يعلم

TABATABAI:6:122#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r2.claim: When faith's spirit settles in a person, it reshapes opinions and deeds to fit it; any settled virtue or vice similarly reshapes thoughts and actions.
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r2.anchor: فإن روح الإيمان إذا تمكنت من نفس الإنسان واستقرت فيها حولت الآراء والأعمال إلى صور تناسبها

TABATABAI:6:122#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r3.claim: The proposal that the light means faith or the Qur'an is unlikely in this context.
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r3.anchor: وربما قيل إن المراد بالنور هو الإيمان أو القرآن وهو بعيد من السياق

TABATABAI:6:122#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r4.claim: The believer uses this light to discern a dark social path, choosing deeds that benefit his happiness and avoiding those that harm it.
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r4.anchor: يتبصر به في مسير حياته الاجتماعية المظلمة ليأخذ من الأعمال ما ينفعه في سعادة حياته

TABATABAI:6:122#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r5.claim: The unbeliever remains in darkness because death does not produce the effects of life; there is no prospect that he will find afterlife-benefiting deeds or salvation.
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r5.anchor: لأن الموت لا يستتبع آثار الحياة البتة فلا مطمع في أن يهتدي الكافر إلى أعمال تنفعه في أخراه

TABATABAI:6:122#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r6.claim: The phrase is elliptical: its estimate is ‘he is in the darknesses, not leaving them,’ with an omitted subject pronoun returning to the relative pronoun.
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r6.anchor: ففي الكلام مبتدأ محذوف هو الضمير العائد إلى الموصول

TABATABAI:6:122#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r7.claim: Another grammatical estimate is ‘like one whose likeness is that of someone in darkness’; al-Tabataba'i accepts it if not for the excessive ellipsis.
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r7.anchor: وقيل التقدير كمن مثله مثل من هو

TABATABAI:6:122#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r8.claim: The simile in ‘thus’ takes the preceding parable as a model and states a general rule, as in the Qur'anic parables of truth and falsehood and of examples.
TABATABAI:6:122#3/r8.anchor: من قبيل تشبيه الفرع بالأصل بعناية إعطاء القاعدة الكلية

TABATABAI:6:122-123/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-123/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122-123/r1.claim: The unbelievers' deeds have been adorned to attract and imprison them in darkness, preventing escape into happiness and light; God does not guide wrongdoers.
TABATABAI:6:122-123/r1.anchor: تجذبهم إليها وتحبسهم ولا تدعهم يخرجوا منها

TABATABAI:6:122-123/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-123/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:6:122-123/r2.claim: A reported reading compares these unbelievers, whose disbelief was adorned, with the earlier believers whose faith was adorned; al-Tabataba'i finds it far from context.
TABATABAI:6:122-123/r2.anchor: وقيل إن وجه التشبيه في قوله

TABATABAI:6:122-123/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-123/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122-123/r4.claim: On this reading, adornment explains why their deeds cannot free them from darkness, while the following verse explains that their plotting harms themselves rather than others.
TABATABAI:6:122-123/r4.anchor: مسوق لبيان أن أعمالهم ومكرهم لا يضر غيرهم

TABATABAI:6:122-123/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-123/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:6:122-123/r5.claim: Another view says God made the disbelievers' deeds attractive and town criminals plot just as He made believers bear light; believers chose guidance, while criminals chose error and were enabled to plot.
TABATABAI:6:122-123/r5.anchor: وقيل معنى التشبيه في الآية أن مثل ذلك

TABATABAI:6:122-127/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r1.claim: Guidance is of two kinds: creational direction of each kind and individual toward its created perfection, acts, appointed course, and lifespan; the Qur'an describes God as giving each thing its form and then guiding it.
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r1.anchor: وهدايته تعالى نوعان أحدهما الهداية التكوينية وهي التي تتعلق بالأمور التكوينية

TABATABAI:6:122-127/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r2.claim: Legislative guidance concerns true beliefs and righteous acts prescribed through commands and prohibitions, with reward promised for obedience and punishment threatened for neglect.
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r2.anchor: والنوع الثاني الهداية التشريعية وهي التي تتعلق بالأمور التشريعية من الاعتقادات الحقة والأعمال الصالحة

TABATABAI:6:122-127/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r3.claim: Legislative guidance can show the road, as in 76:3, or bring someone to the destination, as in 7:176.
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r3.anchor: ومن هذه الهداية ما هي إراءة الطريق كما في قوله تعالى إنا هديناه السبيل

TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r1.claim: In al-Kafi, Zayd says Imam al-Baqir glossed the dead person as one who knows nothing, the light as an imam followed, and the person in darkness as one who does not know the Imam.
TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r1.anchor: عن زيد قال سمعت أبا جعفر عليه السلام يقول

TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabataba'i treats the Imam gloss as an application to a particular case; the context requires life to mean faith and light to mean divine guidance to true belief and righteous action.
TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r2.anchor: أقول وهو من قبيل الجري والانطباق فسياق الآية يأبى إلا أن تكون الحياة هو الإيمان والنور هو الهداية الإلهية

TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r3.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur cites Zayd ibn Aslam as saying the verse was revealed about Ammar ibn Yasir; no grading is stated.
TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم أن الآية نزلت في عمار بن ياسر

TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم
TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r4.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur reports from Ibn Abbas and Zayd ibn Aslam that the verse concerned Umar ibn al-Khattab and Abu Jahl; al-Tabataba'i says the context rules out restricting it to them.
TABATABAI:6:122-127#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم أنها نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب وأبي جهل بن هشام والسياق يأبى كون الآية خاصة

TABRISI:6:122-123/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123/r1.speaker: أهل المدينة ويعقوب
TABRISI:6:122-123/r1.claim: The Medinan readers and Yaʿqūb read maytan with a doubled yāʾ.
TABRISI:6:122-123/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة ويعقوب ميتا بالتشديد

TABRISI:6:122-123/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:6:122-123/r2.claim: The remaining readers use the light pronunciation, without doubling.

TABRISI:6:122-123/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:6:122-123/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats the light form as a shortened form with the same meaning; Abū al-Raʿlā al-Ghassānī's poem calls the despairing living truly dead.
TABRISI:6:122-123/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الميتة تخفيف ميتة

TABRISI:6:122-123/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:122-123/r4.claim: The second of the two yāʾs is deleted; it had changed from wāw and underwent deletion like a letter altered by substitution.
TABRISI:6:122-123/r4.anchor: والمحذوف من الياءين الثانية المنقلبة عن الواو وأعلت بالحذف كما أعلت بالقلب

TABRISI:6:122-123/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:122-123/r7.claim: The interrogative hamza attaches to the conjunction wāw as a rhetorical question seeking acknowledgment.
TABRISI:6:122-123/r7.anchor: أومن هذه همزة الاستفهام دخلت على واو العطف وهو استفهام يراد به التقرير

TABRISI:6:122-123/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:122-123/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the verse came down concerning Ḥamza and Abū Jahl: after Abū Jahl harmed the Prophet, Ḥamza struck him with a bow and embraced Islam.
TABRISI:6:122-123/r9.anchor: نزلت في حمزة بن عبد المطلب وأبي جهل بن هاشم

TABRISI:6:122-123/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123/r10.speaker: عكرمة وأبو جعفر
TABRISI:6:122-123/r10.claim: Another report, from ʿIkrima and transmitted from Abū Jaʿfar, places the occasion in ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir's conversion, contrasted with Abū Jahl.
TABRISI:6:122-123/r10.anchor: في عمار بن ياسر حين آمن وأبي جهل عن عكرمة وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر

TABRISI:6:122-123/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123/r11.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:6:122-123/r11.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the verse was revealed concerning ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
TABRISI:6:122-123/r11.anchor: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب عن الضحاك

TABRISI:6:122-123/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123/r12.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
TABRISI:6:122-123/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan and a group take the verse as a general comparison of every believer and unbeliever; the author prefers this broader reading, which encompasses the specific reports.
TABRISI:6:122-123/r12.anchor: عامة في كل مؤمن وكافر عن الحسن وجماعة وهذا أولى

TABRISI:6:122-123/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123/r13.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد
TABRISI:6:122-123/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Mujāhid explain the dead person as an unbeliever whom God revives by guiding to faith, likening unbelief to death and faith to life.
TABRISI:6:122-123/r13.anchor: أي كافرا فاحييناه بأن هديناه إلى الإيمان عن ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد

TABRISI:6:122-123/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123/r14.speaker: قول غير مسمى
TABRISI:6:122-123/r14.claim: Another view takes the dead person as a sperm drop brought to life, as in the cited verse.
TABRISI:6:122-123/r14.anchor: وقيل: معناه من كان نطفة فأحييناه

TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r1.claim: One explanation is knowledge and wisdom, called light because they guide to right conduct as physical light guides on roads.
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r1.anchor: أحدها: أن المراد بالنور العلم والحكمة

TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies the light as the Qurʾān.
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r2.anchor: وثانيها: إن المراد بالنور هنا القرآن عن مجاهد

TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the light as faith.
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r3.anchor: وثالثها: أن المراد به الإيمان عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r4.claim: A disbeliever is called dead because neither he nor others benefit from his life; unlike the dead, he also incurs punishment and harms others. A believer is alive because his life benefits himself and others.
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r4.anchor: وإنما سمى الله تعالى الكافر ميتا لأنه لا ينتفع بحياته

TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r5.claim: Qurʾān, faith, and knowledge are called light because they guide people from unbelief and confused error as other lights guide the way; unbelief is darkness because it does not guide or disclose right conduct.
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r5.anchor: وسمى القرآن والإيمان والعلم نورا لأن الناس يبصرون بذلك ويهتدون

TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r6.claim: The unbeliever's blindness parallels the images in the verses about one who is blind and the contrast between blind and seeing.
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r6.anchor: وهذا كما سمى الكافر أعمى في قوله:

TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r7.claim: The wording is elliptical: 'like one whose likeness is in darkness' means 'like one who is in darkness'; the expression is framed through the person's likeness.
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r7.anchor: لم يقل سبحانه كمن هو في الظلمات تقديره

TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r8.claim: The comparison is that unbelief was adorned for these people and they practiced it, as faith was adorned for the earlier people and they practiced it; each group's condition is compared in its adornment.
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r8.anchor: معناه زين لهؤلاء الكفر فعملوه مثل ما زين لأولئك الإيمان فعملوه

TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Satan and their own selves adorned their deeds, citing the report that devils inspire their allies.
TABRISI:6:122-123#2/r9.anchor: روي عن الحسن أنه قال زينه والله لهم الشيطان وأنفسهم

TABRISI:6:122-123#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:122-123#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:122-123#3/r1.claim: The passive 'was adorned' does not require an adornment agent distinct from the people, as in the idioms 'he admired himself' and 'he was devoted to this.'
TABRISI:6:122-123#3/r1.anchor: وقوله: { زين } لا يقتضي مزينا غيرهم

THALABI:v4p186/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p186/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p186/r1.claim: The person trapped in darkness sees nothing and cannot find a way out, like someone who loses the road at night.
THALABI:v4p186/r1.anchor: ليس بخارج منها لا يبصر شيئا ولا يعرف طريقا كالذي ضل طريقه في ظلمة الليل

THALABI:v4p186/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p186/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p186/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the dead person brought to life is Hamza and the one in darkness is Abu Jahl; after Abu Jahl stoned the Prophet, Hamza learned of it and converted in anger.
THALABI:v4p186/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: أومن كان [ميتا] فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس. يريد حمزة بن عبد المطلب

THALABI:v4p186/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p186/r3.speaker: الضحاك ويمان
THALABI:v4p186/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak and Yaman say the verse concerns Umar ibn al-Khattab and Abu Jahl.
THALABI:v4p186/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك [ويمان] : نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب وأبي جهل.

THALABI:v4p186/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p186/r4.speaker: عكرمة والكلبي
THALABI:v4p186/r4.claim: Ikrima and al-Kalbi say the verse concerns Ammar ibn Yasir and Abu Jahl.
THALABI:v4p186/r4.anchor: قال عكرمة والكلبي: نزلت في عمار بن ياسر وأبي جهل.

THALABI:v4p186/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p186/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p186/r5.claim: As unbelievers’ deeds are made attractive to them, God likewise makes the criminals in each town its leading figures.
THALABI:v4p186/r5.anchor: وكذلك أي وكما زينا للكافرين أعمالهم كذلك جعلنا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r1.speaker: نافع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r1.claim: Nafi reads mayyitan with a doubled yāʾ; the language authorities say the light and doubled forms have the same meaning.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r2.claim: The light form drops the second yāʾ, which comes from a wāw and was weakened by deletion just as it was weakened by vowel change.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r2.anchor: والمحذوف في (¬5) المخفف من الياءين الثانية المنقلبة عن الواو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد ومحمد بن كعب وجميع المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r3.claim: They interpret the person who was dead and then given life as a disbeliever or astray person whom God guided.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r3.anchor: ومحمد بن كعب (¬2) وجميع المفسرين (¬3): (يعني: من كان كافرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r4.claim: They connect the description of disbelievers as dead to 16:21, then explain ignorance as death and guidance or knowledge as life because they lead to truth and right conduct.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p403/r4.anchor: قد وصف الكفار بأنهم أموات في قوله تعالى: {أموات غير أحياء وما يشعرون أيان يبعثون}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والكلبي وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says religion, Mujahid guidance, al-Kalbi faith among Muslims, and Ibn Zayd Islam; the author treats these glosses as equivalent.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r2.speaker: الزجاج وأبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r2.claim: They say the believer walks among people illuminated by wisdom and faith, meaning the wisdom-light a Muslim receives through Islam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r2.anchor: الزجاج (¬4) وأبو علي (¬5): (المؤمن مستضيء في الناس بنور الحكمة والإيمان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r3.speaker: قتادة والحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r3.claim: Qatada and Hasan identify the light as God's scripture or the Qur'an, which accompanies the believer as the standard by which to act and return.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: (النور هاهنا كتاب الله بينة من الله مع المؤمن، بها يعمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r4.claim: Abu Ali also allows the light to be the light described as running before believers and sought by hypocrites on the Day of Judgment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p404/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي: (ويجوز أن يراد به النور المذكور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r1.claim: The commentators take the person in darkness to be the disbeliever, immersed in unbelief and error.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r2.claim: The wording can mean simply one in darkness: Arabic may add mathal without intending comparison, as in the cited constructions and verses 5:95 and 42:11.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r2.anchor: ولا يريدون به التشبيه، كقولهم: أنا أكرم مثلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r3.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r3.claim: Another reading says the person's likeness is in darkness, so he too is in darkness; the intended referent is the disbeliever himself, not his likeness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r3.anchor: المراد به: الكافر لا شبيهه، وهذان القولان معنى ما ذكره أبو علي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r4.speaker: غيره من النحويين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r4.claim: Other grammarians say mathal is added because the wording makes the person an example of being in darkness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r4.anchor: معنى الآية: كمن في الظلمات، وزيد المثل لأنه يفيد أنه يضرب به المثل في ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r5.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r5.claim: He parses it as someone whose likeness would be likened to one in darkness; al-Wahidi calls this the weakest explanation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r6.claim: Al-Wahidi says mithl and mathal have the same meaning here.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p405/r6.anchor: يمشي به كمن هو في الظلمات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses being unable to leave the darkness as never becoming a believer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r1.anchor: ليس بخارج منها}. قال الكلبي: (ليس بمؤمن أبدا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r2.claim: The commentators agree that the verse was revealed about a believer and a disbeliever, and identify Abu Jahl as the disbeliever.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r2.anchor: واتفق المفسرون على أن هذه الآية نزلت في مؤمن وكافر، وأجمعوا على أن الكافر أبو جهل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the believer as Hamza: after Abu Jahl insulted Muhammad, Hamza confronted him and declared faith, and the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r3.anchor: حمزة بن عبد المطلب، وذلك أن أبا جهل رمى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بفرث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r4.claim: Mujahid says the verse concerns Muhammad and Abu Jahl: Abu Jahl rejected Muhammad out of tribal rivalry and demanded revelation for himself; the account also links 6:124.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: (نزلت في النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأبي جهل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r5.claim: On the report identifying Muhammad and Abu Jahl, Muhammad received guidance, Islam's light, prophethood, and wisdom, while Abu Jahl remained in unbelief's darkness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: (على هذا القول فالنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - هدى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r6.speaker: عكرمة والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r6.claim: Ikrima and al-Kalbi identify the believer as Ammar ibn Yasir and the disbeliever as Abu Jahl.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r6.anchor: وقال عكرمة (¬7) والكلبي (¬8): (نزلت في عمار بن ياسر، وأبي جهل)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r7.speaker: الضحاك ويمان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak and Yaman identify the believer as Umar ibn al-Khattab and the disbeliever as Abu Jahl.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r7.anchor: وقال الضحاك (¬9)، ويمان: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r8.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the verse is general and was not revealed about any particular believer and disbeliever.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن (¬1): (الآية عامة [في كل مؤمن وكافر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r9.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj likewise allows a general reading: every guided person is like the dead revived and lit among people by wisdom and faith, while every disbeliever is trapped in darkness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p407/r9.anchor: وهو قول الزجاج: (يجوز أن تكون هذه الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p409/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p409/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p409/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Satan made idol worship attractive to the disbelievers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p409/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: زين الشيطان لهم عبادة الأصنام)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p409/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p409/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p409/r2.claim: The comparison means their unbelief was made attractive and they acted on it, just as faith was made attractive to the believers; their cases are likened in this adornment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p409/r2.anchor: فشبهت حال هؤلاء في التزيين بحال أولئك فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p409/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p409/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p409/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq assigns the kāf the syntactic position of nominative: the meaning is that the like of what was recounted was made attractive to the disbelievers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p409/r3.anchor: موضع الكاف رفع، المعنى: مثل ذلك الذي قصصنا عليك زين للكافرين عملهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p159#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p159#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p159#3/r1.claim: The dead person in the comparison was an unbeliever whom God guided; the light is faith, and walking by it means being guided, while darkness represents unbelief.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p159#3/r1.anchor: أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه} أي: كان كافرا فهديناه. {وجعلنا له نورا} إيمانا.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r1.claim: The dead person was a misguided unbeliever whom God guided; the light is religion and faith.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r1.anchor: { أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه } ضالا كافرا فهديناه { وجعلنا له نورا } دينا وإيمانا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r2.claim: He walks among Muslims, lit by the wisdom and faith God casts into his heart.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r2.anchor: { يمشي به في الناس } مع المسلمين مستضيئا بما قذف الله في قلبه من نور الحكمة والإيمان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r3.claim: The comparison is with someone in the darkness of unbelief and error who will never believe.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r3.anchor: { كمن مثله } كمن هو { في الظلمات } في ظلمات الكفر والضلالة { ليس بخارج منها } ليس بمؤمن أبدا.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r4.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r4.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل وحمزة بن عبد المطلب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r5.claim: As faith was made attractive to believers, idol worship was made attractive to unbelievers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:122-123/r5.anchor: { كذلك } كما زين للمؤمنين الإيمان { زين للكافرين ما كانوا يعملون } من عبادة الأصنام.

ELMALILI:6:122/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:122/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:122/r1.claim: In his rendering, bi’t-temsîl makes the comparison explicit and yaldızlı (“gilded”) renders the disbelievers’ deeds as coated or prettified.
ELMALILI:6:122/r1.anchor: hiç o bi’t-temsîl zulmetler içinde kalmış ve ondan bir türlü çıkamayacak bir hâlde bulunan kimse gibi olur mu?

ELMALILI:6:122/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:122/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:122/r2.claim: The wording recalls 6:108, where God says that each community’s deeds were made fair to it; the beautification here follows the same pattern.
ELMALILI:6:122/r2.anchor: Yani bâlâda كَذَٰلِكَ زَيَّنَّا لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ عَمَلَهُمْ [el-En‘âm 6/108] buyurulmamış mı idi?

ELMALILI:6:122/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:122/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:122/r3.claim: The beautification comes from devils through their misleading promptings and from God in the sense that He creates those promptings as they occur.
ELMALILI:6:122/r3.anchor: Şeytanların yaldızlı ilkāâtı itibariyle şeytanlar tarafından ve o ilkāât esnasında halk tarîkiyle de Allah tarafındandır.

ELMALILI:6:122/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:122/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:122/r4.claim: Because their deeds are beautified, disbelievers approve of what they do and cannot leave the darkness.
ELMALILI:6:122/r4.anchor: Ve bu tezyin yüzündendir ki kâfirler yaptıklarını beğenir ve zulumâttan çıkamazlar.

ELMALILI:6:122/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:122/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:122/r5.claim: The warning about beautified deeds and remaining in darkness is not confined to the Meccans.
ELMALILI:6:122/r5.anchor: Hem bu yalnız Mekkelilere mahsus da değildir:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r1.claim: After 6:121 describes polytheists fighting believers under satanic prompting, this verse contrasts the two groups through a vivid parable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r1.anchor: Bir önceki âyette müşriklerin, şeytanların telkinleri altında müminlere karşı mücadele açmasından söz edildikten sonra bu âyette, belirtilen iki kesimin durumu parlak bir temsille değerlendirilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r2.claim: The pre-Islamic state of believers is likened to death, since unbelief and associating partners with God deprive a person of good and block discerning truth and finding salvation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r2.anchor: müminlerin İslâm’ı kabul etmelerinden önceki durumu, bir ölü gibi bütünüyle hayır ve faydadan yoksun kalmış olanın durumuna benzetilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r3.claim: The person granted Islam is revived and gains light in heart and mind to distinguish truth from falsehood and benefit from harm, which also lights the way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r3.anchor: gerçeği gerçek olmayandan, doğru ve yararlı olanı yanlış ve zararlı olandan ayırt etme imkânına kavuşmuştur; böylece iman nuruyla zihni ve kalbi aydınlanan kişinin bu sayede yolu da aydınlık olur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r4.claim: For one fixed in disbelief, there is no hope of escaping darkness while disbelief continues.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r4.anchor: İnkâra saplanmış olan için ise, küfrü devam ettiği sürece karanlıktan kurtuluş ümidi de kalmamıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r5.claim: As 6:121 indicates, satanic suggestions undermine disbelievers’ reasoning and evaluation until their bad deeds appear attractive to them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:122/r5.anchor: 121. âyette belirtildiği üzere inkârcılar, şeytanların telkin ettiği vesveselerle muhâkeme ve değerlendirme disiplinlerini kaybettikleri için yaptıkları çirkin işler de artık kendilerine güzel gösterilmiştir.

ITQAN:v3p211/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p211/r2.speaker: ثعلب والمبرد
ITQAN:v3p211/r2.claim: They say a negation at the start of a sentence is genuine negation, as in “Mā Zayd bi-khārij,” and distinguish it from paired negatives.
ITQAN:v3p211/r2.anchor: وإذا كان الجحد في أول الكلام كان جحدا حقيقيا نحو ( ما زيد بخارج )

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r1.claim: The verse metaphorically calls ignorance death and knowledge of God and revelation life, with the light of faith replacing the prior state of spiritual death.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r1.anchor: جعل من حصل له العلم بعد أن لم يكن كأنه إنما وجد الحياة وصارت صفة له مع وجود نور الإيمان في قلبه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r2.claim: ‘Alive of heart’ may mean intellectually alert and discerning truth from falsehood, or active and quick to act; the latter sense also applies to animals.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r2.anchor: فلان حي القلب يريدون أنه ثاقب الفهم جيد النظر مستعد لتمييز الحق من الباطل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r3.claim: Life can stand for knowledge or ability, and death for their absence or weakness, since both knowledge and power distinguish the living.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r3.anchor: صار إطلاق الحياة مرة عبارة عن العلم وأخرى عن القدرة وإطلاق الموت إشارة إلى عدم القدرة وضعفها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r4.claim: Treating existence as nonexistence is a conventional intensifier of disparagement; poets may exaggerate further by placing something below nonexistence.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r4.anchor: تنزيل الوجود منزلة العدم إذا أريد المبالغة في حط الشىء والوضع منه وخروجه عن أن يعتد به

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r5.claim: A second way to praise is to make the honored person uniquely ‘the thing,’ as in ‘this is the thing and all else is not,’ thereby maximizing distinction.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p58/r5.anchor: أحدهما أن يريد المدح واثبات المزية والفضل على غاية المبالغة حتى لا يحصل عليه مزيدا فإذا أردت ذلك جعلت الإثبات كأنه مقصور عليه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r1.claim: In phrases such as days causing gray hair, the metaphor lies in attributing the real effect to days; the gray hair itself remains real.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r1.anchor: المجاز واقع في اثبات الشيب فعلا للأيام ولكر الليالي وهو الذي أزيل عن موضعه الذي ينبغي أن يكون فيه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r2.claim: Here metaphor lies in the predicate ‘life,’ meaning knowledge, guidance, and wisdom for hearts; attributing this gift to God is literal.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r2.anchor: فالمجاز في المثبت وهو الحياة فأما الإثبات فواقع على حقيقته لأنه ينصرف إلى أن الهدى والعلم والحكمة فضل من الله

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r4.claim: A phrase can be figurative in both predicate and attribution: ‘your sight revived me’ first calls delight life, then makes the sight its agent.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r4.anchor: جعل الأنس والمسرة الحاصلة بالرؤية حياة أولا ثم جعل الرؤية فاعلة لتلك الحياة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r1.claim: If an added particle causes an unexpected grammatical case, that case can be figurative: in ‘ليس كمثله شيء,’ the added kāf makes مثل genitive instead of its original accusative.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r1.anchor: فإن حدث هناك بسبب ذلك الزائد حكم تزول به الكلمة عن أصلها جاز حينئذ أن يوصف ذلك الحكم أو ما وقع فيه بأنه مجاز

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r2.claim: Addition alone is not metaphor: metaphor transfers a word to another meaning, while an element with no intended meaning has undergone no such transfer.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r2.anchor: قولنا المجاز يفيد أن تجوز بالكلمة موضعها في أصل الوضع وتنقلها عن دلالة إلى دلالة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r3.speaker: أبو علي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī allows a word to count from one perspective and be disregarded from another, such as the lām in ‘لا أبا لزيد.’
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r3.anchor: يقول الشيخ أبو علي في الكلمة إذا كانت تزول عن أصلها من وجه ولا تزول من آخر معتد بها من وجه غير معتد بها من وجه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r4.claim: In ‘لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب,’ لا may be extra in the direct negation but meaningful as emphasis of the following negation; its status depends on the aspect considered.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p363/r4.anchor: لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب أن لا يقدرون ^

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p104/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p104/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p104/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the image of one who was dead and then given life was revealed about ʿUmar and Abū Jahl; al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports the same.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p104/r1.anchor: أخرج أبو الشيخ عن ابن عباس في قوله ﴿ أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه ﴾ قال نزلت في عمر وأبي جهل

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p224/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p224/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p224/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the enlivened person as Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib and the one in darkness as Abu Jahl: after Hamza learned that Abu Jahl had abused Muhammad, he confronted him and embraced Islam, and the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p224/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد حمزة بن عبد المطلب وأبا جهل، وذلك أن أبا جهل رمى رسول الله

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p224/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p224/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p224/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies the person given light as Umar ibn al-Khattab and the person remaining in darkness as Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p224/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم في قوله - عز وجل - {أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا

DAMGHANI:v1p466/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p466/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p466/r3.claim: Nūr can mean faith that guides a person; the other examples equate it with faith and the move from disbelief to belief.
DAMGHANI:v1p466/r3.anchor: الثاني النور الإيمان قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r4.claim: A third sense is guidance: the guided person is described as alive.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحياة في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r1.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r1.claim: Alī b. ʿUbayd Allāh defines light as radiant illumination that lets sight reach visible objects and grows with its causes.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r1.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله . النور : هو الضياء المتشعشع الذي تنفذه أنوار الأبصار

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r2.claim: The word comes from fire; nāra, anāra, and istanāra describe something becoming bright.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r2.anchor: والنور مأخوذ من النار ، يقال تنورت النار : إذا قصدت نحوها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r3.claim: Light is used figuratively for clarification: a person can make speech clear; manār can mean landmarks and boundaries.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r3.anchor: ثم يستعار في مواضع تدل عليها القرينة فيقال : أنار فلان كلامه إذا أوضحه . ومنار الأرض : أعلامها وحدودها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r4.claim: Manāra is derived on the pattern mafʿala from istināra.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r6.claim: Light can mean faith, as in the light given to a person who walks among people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p599/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن النور في القرآن على عشرة أوجه : -

BURHAN:v2p346/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p346/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p346/r2.claim: Other comparisons state both sides explicitly, as in the examples of the dead person given life and the person with proof compared with one whose deeds are beautified.
BURHAN:v2p346/r2.anchor: وجاء مصرحا بهما على الاصل في قوله تعالى ﴿ أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به

ITQAN:v3p124/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p124/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p124/r3.claim: A concordant metaphor joins meanings that can coexist: making someone alive represents guiding the lost, and life and guidance could meet in one thing.
ITQAN:v3p124/r3.anchor: أي ضالا فهديناه استعير الإحياء من جعل الشيء حيا للهداية

ITQAN:v2p310/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p310/r18.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p310/r18.claim: “Dead, then We revived him” means astray, then We guided him.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r5.claim: Mawt can mean misguidance, from which God brings a person into life and guidance.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r5.anchor: والثالث : الضلال . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p90/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p90/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p90/r8.claim: Death is disbelief and being brought to life is guidance; the light is faith guiding toward good and salvation, while darkness represents disbelief.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p90/r8.anchor: أى كان كافرا فهديناه وجعلنا له ايمانا يهتدى به سبل الخير والنجاة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r11.claim: God explicitly ascribes beautifying faith and the adorned heavens to Himself; beautification of worldly desires and sinful deeds is generally passive, and the text does not say ‘We beautified their evil deeds.’
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r11.anchor: فأنت ترى أنه ينسب تزيين الخير إلى نفسه بخلاف تزيين السوء

DAMGHANI:v1p436/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p436/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p436/r1.claim: Walking with the light means being guided by it; 57:28 similarly describes believers walking by a light of faith and guidance.
DAMGHANI:v1p436/r1.anchor: الثانى : المشى الهدى . قوله تعالى فى سورة النعام
